rfcs.applies_when: The content trains, evaluates, registers, deploys or monitors a machine learning model, defines model features, or describes such a model.
rfcs.not_applies_when: No machine learning model or model feature is trained, evaluated, served or described.
rfcs.summary: Reproducible training, honest evaluation, bias checks, registration and production monitoring of machine learning models such as ranking and no-show prediction.
rfcs.title: Machine learning model lifecycle

rfcs.applies_when: The content is or changes Java or Kotlin backend source code of a Spring Boot service.
rfcs.not_applies_when: The content is not Java or Kotlin backend source code, or is Android app code.
rfcs.summary: Conventions for Spring Boot backend code in Java and Kotlin: dependency injection, transaction boundaries, null safety and blocking calls in reactive code.
rfcs.title: Spring Boot services in Java and Kotlin

rfcs.applies_when: The content is or changes Go source code (.go files) of a service, worker or command-line tool.
rfcs.not_applies_when: The content is not Go source code.
rfcs.summary: Conventions for Go service code: context propagation, error wrapping, goroutine lifetimes and closing resources.
rfcs.title: Go services

rfcs.applies_when: The content adds or changes a product analytics event (Amplitude, Segment, GA, Firebase), a tracking call, or a data export, report download or data share that contains data about diners or restaurant staff.
rfcs.not_applies_when: No analytics event, tracking call, data export or data share is added, changed or described.
rfcs.summary: What personal data can appear in product analytics events and in data exports to partners, restaurants and internal teams, and how it is pseudonymised and limited.
rfcs.title: Personal data in analytics events and data exports

statements.applies_when: the content adds a route, controller method or handler, or marks a route as public or anonymous (for example `@PermitAll`, `permitAll()`, `auth: false`).
statements.not_applies_when: No HTTP endpoint, route, gateway rule or request middleware is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Every new route MUST require an authenticated caller unless it is listed in the service's public-route allowlist with a comment giving the reason.
statements.title: Authenticated by default

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes a handler that reads a resource id such as `reservationId`, `restaurantId` or `userId` from the request and loads or updates that record.
statements.not_applies_when: No HTTP endpoint, route, gateway rule or request middleware is added, changed or described.
statements.text: A handler that loads a resource by an identifier from the path or body MUST check that the authenticated caller owns or is granted access to that specific resource before returning or changing it.
statements.title: Object-level authorization

statements.applies_when: the content decodes, parses or verifies a JWT or bearer token, or configures a JWT validator or auth middleware.
statements.not_applies_when: No HTTP endpoint, route, gateway rule or request middleware is added, changed or described.
statements.text: A service that accepts a bearer JWT MUST verify its signature, issuer, audience and expiry, and MUST reject tokens signed with the `none` algorithm.
statements.title: Token validation

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes an operation in an OpenAPI or Swagger file.
statements.not_applies_when: No HTTP endpoint, route, gateway rule or request middleware is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Each operation in an OpenAPI document MUST declare its `security` requirement and the OAuth scopes or roles it needs.
statements.title: Scopes declared in the contract

statements.applies_when: the content adds a route to the public or partner API gateway configuration, or adds an endpoint documented for partners or public clients.
statements.not_applies_when: No HTTP endpoint, route, gateway rule or request middleware is added, changed or described.
statements.text: A route exposed through the public or partner gateway MUST have a per-client rate limit configured at the gateway or in the service.
statements.title: Rate limit on public and partner routes

statements.applies_when: the content implements or configures the response returned when a rate limit or quota is exceeded.
statements.not_applies_when: No HTTP endpoint, route, gateway rule or request middleware is added, changed or described.
statements.text: A request rejected by a rate limiter MUST get status 429 with a `Retry-After` header.
statements.title: Rate limit responses

statements.applies_when: the content chooses the key, bucket or identifier used by a rate limiter.
statements.not_applies_when: No HTTP endpoint, route, gateway rule or request middleware is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Rate limits SHOULD be keyed on the authenticated client id or API key, and SHOULD use the client IP only for anonymous routes.
statements.title: Rate limit key

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes rate limiting on a partner-facing endpoint or its response headers.
statements.not_applies_when: No HTTP endpoint, route, gateway rule or request middleware is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Responses from partner APIs SHOULD include `RateLimit-Limit`, `RateLimit-Remaining` and `RateLimit-Reset` headers so clients can pace their calls.
statements.title: Rate limit headers

statements.applies_when: the content adds authentication between two internal services, or configures a static API key or shared header for an internal caller.
statements.not_applies_when: No HTTP endpoint, route, gateway rule or request middleware is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Internal service-to-service calls MUST authenticate with the mesh workload identity or a short-lived service token, not with a shared static API key.
statements.title: Service-to-service identity

statements.applies_when: the content adds or configures a login, password reset, search or bulk export endpoint.
statements.not_applies_when: No HTTP endpoint, route, gateway rule or request middleware is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Login, search and export routes MAY have a separate, lower rate limit than the default for the same client.
statements.title: Stricter limits on expensive routes

statements.applies_when: the content builds or sends an outgoing webhook request to a partner or customer URL.
statements.not_applies_when: No webhook is sent or received and no endpoint starts an asynchronous job or operation.
statements.text: Every outgoing webhook MUST carry an HMAC-SHA256 signature of the raw body and a timestamp in request headers, computed with a secret specific to that subscription.
statements.title: Signed webhook payloads

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes an endpoint that receives webhooks or callbacks from a third party (payment provider, POS vendor, messaging provider).
statements.not_applies_when: No webhook is sent or received and no endpoint starts an asynchronous job or operation.
statements.text: A handler for an incoming webhook MUST verify the provider's signature on the raw body and MUST reject requests whose timestamp is older than five minutes.
statements.title: Verify incoming webhooks

statements.applies_when: the content defines or changes the payload body of an outgoing webhook.
statements.not_applies_when: No webhook is sent or received and no endpoint starts an asynchronous job or operation.
statements.text: Each webhook payload MUST include a unique event id and an event type so receivers can deduplicate deliveries.
statements.title: Webhook event identity

statements.applies_when: the content sends an HTTP request to a subscriber URL inside a request handler, transaction or domain service.
statements.not_applies_when: No webhook is sent or received and no endpoint starts an asynchronous job or operation.
statements.text: Webhook delivery MUST run from a queue or outbox worker, not inline in the request that caused the event.
statements.title: Delivery off the request path

statements.applies_when: the content implements or configures retry, dead-lettering or disabling of webhook deliveries.
statements.not_applies_when: No webhook is sent or received and no endpoint starts an asynchronous job or operation.
statements.text: Failed webhook deliveries SHOULD be retried for at least 24 hours, and a subscription SHOULD be disabled with a notification to its owner after repeated failure over three days.
statements.title: Redelivery and disabling

statements.applies_when: the content registers, validates or stores a webhook subscription or callback URL supplied by a customer.
statements.not_applies_when: No webhook is sent or received and no endpoint starts an asynchronous job or operation.
statements.text: Webhook subscription URLs MUST use HTTPS and MUST NOT resolve to private, loopback or link-local addresses.
statements.title: Subscriber URL validation

statements.applies_when: the content adds an endpoint that starts an export, import, bulk update, report generation or other long-running job.
statements.not_applies_when: No webhook is sent or received and no endpoint starts an asynchronous job or operation.
statements.text: An endpoint that starts work expected to take longer than two seconds SHOULD return 202 with a `Location` header pointing to an operation status resource.
statements.title: Accepted status for long operations

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes an endpoint that reports the status of an asynchronous job or operation.
statements.not_applies_when: No webhook is sent or received and no endpoint starts an asynchronous job or operation.
statements.text: An operation status resource MUST expose a state from a fixed set (`pending`, `running`, `succeeded`, `failed`) and, when finished, a link to the result or an error.
statements.title: Operation status resource

statements.applies_when: the content designs or implements the request body of an endpoint that starts a long-running job.
statements.not_applies_when: No webhook is sent or received and no endpoint starts an asynchronous job or operation.
statements.text: A long-running operation MAY accept a callback URL so the client is notified on completion instead of polling.
statements.title: Callback instead of polling

statements.applies_when: the content sets a cookie that holds a session id, access token or refresh token (`Set-Cookie`, `res.cookie`, `ResponseCookie`).
statements.not_applies_when: No login, password, session, cookie or refresh token logic is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Session and refresh-token cookies MUST be set with `Secure`, `HttpOnly` and `SameSite=Lax` or `SameSite=Strict`.
statements.title: Session cookie attributes

statements.applies_when: the content implements the success path of a login, a role switch or an impersonation start.
statements.not_applies_when: No login, password, session, cookie or refresh token logic is added, changed or described.
statements.text: The session identifier MUST be regenerated after a successful login and after a privilege change such as switching to a restaurant admin role.
statements.title: Session rotation on login

statements.applies_when: the content implements a logout endpoint, a sign-out action or token revocation.
statements.not_applies_when: No login, password, session, cookie or refresh token logic is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Logout MUST invalidate the session or refresh token on the server, not only delete the cookie or local storage entry on the client.
statements.title: Server-side logout

statements.applies_when: the content configures session timeouts, refresh-token lifetimes or remember-me duration.
statements.not_applies_when: No login, password, session, cookie or refresh token logic is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Diner sessions SHOULD expire after 30 days of inactivity and back-office sessions SHOULD expire after 8 hours of inactivity.
statements.title: Session lifetime

statements.applies_when: the content implements or changes a login, one-time-code verification or password check endpoint.
statements.not_applies_when: No login, password, session, cookie or refresh token logic is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Failed login attempts MUST be throttled per account and per source IP, with a growing delay or a temporary lock after 10 failures in 15 minutes.
statements.title: Login throttling

statements.applies_when: the content writes the error or success message of a login, sign-up or password reset flow.
statements.not_applies_when: No login, password, session, cookie or refresh token logic is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Login and password reset responses MUST NOT reveal whether an email address has an account.
statements.title: Uniform login errors

statements.applies_when: the content generates, stores or checks a password reset or magic-link token.
statements.not_applies_when: No login, password, session, cookie or refresh token logic is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Password reset tokens MUST be single-use, random with at least 128 bits of entropy, and expire within one hour.
statements.title: Password reset tokens

statements.applies_when: the content adds a login path or authentication provider for an internal tool, admin console or back-office application.
statements.not_applies_when: No login, password, session, cookie or refresh token logic is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Back-office and restaurant admin accounts MUST sign in through the corporate SSO with multi-factor authentication enforced.
statements.title: MFA for back-office

statements.applies_when: the content implements an endpoint or screen that changes a user's email, password, phone number or payout details.
statements.not_applies_when: No login, password, session, cookie or refresh token logic is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Changing an email address, password or payout bank details SHOULD require the user to re-enter their password or a fresh one-time code.
statements.title: Re-authentication for sensitive changes

statements.applies_when: the content designs or implements a new diner login or sign-up method.
statements.not_applies_when: No login, password, session, cookie or refresh token logic is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Diner login MAY offer WebAuthn passkeys as an alternative to a password.
statements.title: Passkeys

statements.applies_when: the content hashes, stores or compares a user password or PIN.
statements.not_applies_when: No hashing, encryption, signing, random token generation or TLS configuration is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Passwords MUST be hashed with Argon2id, or with bcrypt at cost 12 or higher for existing stores, and MUST NOT be hashed with MD5, SHA-1 or unsalted SHA-256.
statements.title: Password hashing algorithm

statements.applies_when: the content generates a token, code, nonce, salt or id used for authentication, authorization or unguessable links.
statements.not_applies_when: No hashing, encryption, signing, random token generation or TLS configuration is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Tokens, reset codes, session ids and nonces MUST be generated with a cryptographically secure generator (`crypto.randomBytes`, `secrets`, `SecureRandom`, `crypto/rand`).
statements.title: Secure random generator

statements.applies_when: the content calls `Math.random`, `random.random`, `random.randint`, `random.choice`, `kotlin.random.Random` or `java.util.Random`.
statements.not_applies_when: No hashing, encryption, signing, random token generation or TLS configuration is added, changed or described.
statements.text: `Math.random()`, Python `random` and `java.util.Random` MUST NOT be used for any security-relevant value.
statements.title: Banned random functions

statements.applies_when: the content encrypts or decrypts data with a symmetric cipher, or chooses a cipher mode, key size or IV.
statements.not_applies_when: No hashing, encryption, signing, random token generation or TLS configuration is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Symmetric encryption MUST use an authenticated mode such as AES-256-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305, with a unique random nonce for each message.
statements.title: Authenticated encryption

statements.applies_when: the content implements bitwise encryption logic, custom padding, XOR obfuscation or a hand-written signature scheme.
statements.not_applies_when: No hashing, encryption, signing, random token generation or TLS configuration is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Code MUST use the platform library or the shared `crypto-kit` wrappers, and MUST NOT implement its own cipher, padding scheme or signature algorithm.
statements.title: No custom cryptography

statements.applies_when: the content compares a received signature, HMAC, API token or reset code with an expected value.
statements.not_applies_when: No hashing, encryption, signing, random token generation or TLS configuration is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Signatures, MACs and tokens MUST be compared with a constant-time function (`hmac.compare_digest`, `crypto.timingSafeEqual`, `MessageDigest.isEqual`).
statements.title: Constant-time comparison

statements.applies_when: the content creates, loads or stores an encryption key for data at rest, or encrypts a database column or file.
statements.not_applies_when: No hashing, encryption, signing, random token generation or TLS configuration is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Encryption keys for data at rest SHOULD be data keys wrapped by the cloud KMS, so that the key-encryption key never leaves the KMS.
statements.title: Keys from KMS

statements.applies_when: the content configures TLS versions, cipher suites or certificate verification (`verify=False`, `rejectUnauthorized: false`, `InsecureSkipVerify`).
statements.not_applies_when: No hashing, encryption, signing, random token generation or TLS configuration is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Servers and clients SHOULD accept TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3 only, and SHOULD NOT disable certificate verification outside local tests.
statements.title: TLS versions

statements.applies_when: the content hashes an email, phone number or other personal identifier to build a lookup key or analytics id.
statements.not_applies_when: No hashing, encryption, signing, random token generation or TLS configuration is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Pseudonymous identifiers derived from emails or phone numbers SHOULD use a keyed HMAC-SHA256 rather than a plain hash, so they cannot be reversed with a dictionary.
statements.title: Hashing for identifiers

statements.applies_when: the content hashes data only to build a cache key, detect duplicates or check file integrity in transit.
statements.not_applies_when: No hashing, encryption, signing, random token generation or TLS configuration is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Non-security checksums such as cache keys or file deduplication MAY use fast hashes like xxHash or CRC32.
statements.title: Checksums

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes a package manifest, a lock file, or an install command in a build script.
statements.not_applies_when: No package manifest, lock file or registry configuration is added or changed.
statements.text: Every service and library MUST commit its lock file, and CI MUST install from the lock file without updating it (`npm ci`, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `uv sync --locked`).
statements.title: Lock files committed

statements.applies_when: the content changes `.npmrc`, `pip.conf`, `uv` index settings, Gradle repositories, `GOPROXY`, or adds a dependency pointing to a Git URL or tarball.
statements.not_applies_when: No package manifest, lock file or registry configuration is added or changed.
statements.text: Packages MUST be resolved through the company Artifactory proxy, not directly from public registries or Git URLs.
statements.title: Internal registry proxy

statements.applies_when: the content adds a new dependency or changes a dependency version.
statements.not_applies_when: No package manifest, lock file or registry configuration is added or changed.
statements.text: A change MUST NOT add or upgrade to a dependency version with a known critical or high vulnerability that has a fixed version available.
statements.title: No known critical vulnerabilities

statements.applies_when: the content adds a new direct dependency to a package manifest.
statements.not_applies_when: No package manifest, lock file or registry configuration is added or changed.
statements.text: A pull request that adds a new direct dependency SHOULD state why it is needed and why an existing dependency or the standard library does not cover it.
statements.title: New dependency justification

statements.applies_when: the content adds a new direct dependency to a package manifest.
statements.not_applies_when: No package manifest, lock file or registry configuration is added or changed.
statements.text: A new direct dependency SHOULD have a compatible open-source license (no AGPL or unlicensed packages), a release in the last 18 months and more than one maintainer.
statements.title: Package health

statements.applies_when: the content adds an npm or pnpm dependency, or changes `onlyBuiltDependencies`, `ignore-scripts` or similar install-script settings.
statements.not_applies_when: No package manifest, lock file or registry configuration is added or changed.
statements.text: Packages that run install or postinstall scripts MUST be listed in the repository's allowlist of trusted build scripts before they are added.
statements.title: Install scripts

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes a `uses:` line in a GitHub Actions workflow or a `FROM` line in a Dockerfile.
statements.not_applies_when: No package manifest, lock file or registry configuration is added or changed.
statements.text: Third-party GitHub Actions MUST be pinned to a full commit SHA, and container base images MUST be pinned by digest.
statements.title: Pinned GitHub Actions and base images

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes `renovate.json`, Dependabot configuration or a new repository skeleton.
statements.not_applies_when: No package manifest, lock file or registry configuration is added or changed.
statements.text: Repositories SHOULD enable Renovate with grouped minor and patch updates and a weekly schedule.
statements.title: Automated update bot

statements.applies_when: the content adds source code copied from an external project into a `vendor`, `third_party` or `lib` folder.
statements.not_applies_when: No package manifest, lock file or registry configuration is added or changed.
statements.text: Copied third-party source files MUST keep their original license header and a note giving the upstream project and version.
statements.title: Vendored code

statements.applies_when: the content changes the release build of a service or adds SBOM generation.
statements.not_applies_when: No package manifest, lock file or registry configuration is added or changed.
statements.text: Services MAY publish a CycloneDX SBOM as a build artifact for each release.
statements.title: SBOM publication

statements.applies_when: the content defines a new metric name in code or configuration.
statements.not_applies_when: No metric is created, recorded or configured.
statements.text: Metric names MUST be lowercase, dot-separated and start with the service or domain prefix, for example `booking.reservation.created`.
statements.title: Metric name format

statements.applies_when: the content records a duration, size, amount or other measured value as a metric.
statements.not_applies_when: No metric is created, recorded or configured.
statements.text: Metrics that measure a quantity with a unit MUST put the base unit as the last name part, such as `_seconds`, `_bytes` or `_ms`, and MUST use the same unit across the service.
statements.title: Unit in the name

statements.applies_when: the content adds a tag or label to a metric, or builds a tag value from request data.
statements.not_applies_when: No metric is created, recorded or configured.
statements.text: Metric tags MUST NOT contain user ids, reservation ids, emails, raw URLs, request ids or other values with unbounded cardinality.
statements.title: No unbounded tags

statements.applies_when: the content tags a request metric with a path, route or endpoint value.
statements.not_applies_when: No metric is created, recorded or configured.
statements.text: HTTP metrics MUST tag the route template (`/restaurants/{id}`) and never the concrete path.
statements.title: Route templates, not paths

statements.applies_when: the content adds a metric with several tags, or tags with values taken from a list that grows over time (restaurants, cities, partners).
statements.not_applies_when: No metric is created, recorded or configured.
statements.text: A new metric SHOULD stay below 1,000 unique tag combinations per service, and a design that expects more SHOULD state the estimate and get SRE approval.
statements.title: Cardinality budget

statements.applies_when: the content records a duration, latency or response time as a metric.
statements.not_applies_when: No metric is created, recorded or configured.
statements.text: Latencies MUST be recorded as histograms or distributions, not as gauges or averages computed in the application.
statements.title: Latency as histograms

statements.applies_when: the content adds metrics counting successes, failures or occurrences of an event.
statements.not_applies_when: No metric is created, recorded or configured.
statements.text: Events that happen (bookings created, payments failed) SHOULD be counters with an outcome tag instead of separate metrics for success and failure.
statements.title: Counters for events

statements.applies_when: the content configures a metrics client, a StatsD or OpenTelemetry meter provider, or sets global metric tags.
statements.not_applies_when: No metric is created, recorded or configured.
statements.text: Every metric MUST carry the `service`, `env` and `version` tags set by the shared telemetry library rather than by hand.
statements.title: Standard tags

statements.applies_when: the content deletes a metric, renames it or changes its tags.
statements.not_applies_when: No metric is created, recorded or configured.
statements.text: Removing or renaming a metric SHOULD be preceded by a search for dashboards and monitors that use it, and the pull request SHOULD list them.
statements.title: Removing metrics

statements.applies_when: the content adds a metric that counts a business event like bookings, covers, reviews or payouts.
statements.not_applies_when: No metric is created, recorded or configured.
statements.text: Services MAY emit business counters such as covers booked per market, provided the tags stay within the cardinality budget.
statements.title: Business metrics

statements.applies_when: the content creates an HTTP or gRPC client, or configures a propagator for a tracer.
statements.not_applies_when: No span, tracer or trace context propagation is created, changed or configured.
statements.text: Services MUST propagate trace context with the W3C `traceparent` and `tracestate` headers on every outbound HTTP and gRPC call.
statements.title: W3C trace context

statements.applies_when: the content produces or consumes Kafka or queue messages in a service that has tracing enabled.
statements.not_applies_when: No span, tracer or trace context propagation is created, changed or configured.
statements.text: Producers MUST write the trace context into Kafka message headers, and consumers MUST start their processing span as a child or link of that context.
statements.title: Context in messages

statements.applies_when: the content creates a span or sets a span name or resource name.
statements.not_applies_when: No span, tracer or trace context propagation is created, changed or configured.
statements.text: Span names MUST be low-cardinality, such as `GET /restaurants/{id}` or `ReservationService.confirm`, and MUST NOT contain ids or query strings.
statements.title: Span names

statements.applies_when: the content sets attributes or tags on a span.
statements.not_applies_when: No span, tracer or trace context propagation is created, changed or configured.
statements.text: Span attributes SHOULD use the OpenTelemetry semantic convention names (`http.request.method`, `db.system`, `messaging.destination.name`) instead of custom names for the same thing.
statements.title: Semantic conventions

statements.applies_when: the content sets span attributes, span events or baggage from request, user or database data.
statements.not_applies_when: No span, tracer or trace context propagation is created, changed or configured.
statements.text: Span attributes and span events MUST NOT contain names, emails, phone numbers, full request bodies or SQL with literal values.
statements.title: No personal data in spans

statements.applies_when: the content catches an exception or error inside code that has an active or manually created span.
statements.not_applies_when: No span, tracer or trace context propagation is created, changed or configured.
statements.text: When an operation fails, the span MUST be marked with error status and the exception recorded on it before the span ends.
statements.title: Errors recorded on spans

statements.applies_when: the content calls `startSpan`, `start_span`, `spanBuilder().startSpan()` or `tracer.Start` directly.
statements.not_applies_when: No span, tracer or trace context propagation is created, changed or configured.
statements.text: Manually started spans MUST be ended in a `finally` block or with a scoped helper (`with tracer.start_as_current_span`, `span.use {}`, `defer span.End()`).
statements.title: Spans always ended

statements.applies_when: the content configures a sampler, sampling rate or trace exporter in a service.
statements.not_applies_when: No span, tracer or trace context propagation is created, changed or configured.
statements.text: Services SHOULD send all spans to the local collector and leave sampling decisions to the collector's tail-sampling policy.
statements.title: Sampling at the collector

statements.applies_when: the content creates spans inside a loop or around small in-process functions.
statements.not_applies_when: No span, tracer or trace context propagation is created, changed or configured.
statements.text: Code SHOULD NOT create a manual span for each loop iteration or for in-memory functions that take less than a millisecond.
statements.title: Span granularity

statements.applies_when: the content adds a business identifier as a span attribute.
statements.not_applies_when: No span, tracer or trace context propagation is created, changed or configured.
statements.text: Spans MAY carry a small set of business attributes such as `restaurant.id` or `booking.channel` to help debugging, as long as they contain no personal data.
statements.title: Business identifiers

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes a call to another service or third party from search, availability, booking or checkout code.
statements.not_applies_when: No circuit breaker, bulkhead, concurrency limit or load shedding is configured and no dependency is called.
statements.text: Calls to a remote dependency on the search, availability or booking path MUST go through a circuit breaker (Resilience4j, `opossum`, `gobreaker` or the shared client wrapper).
statements.title: Circuit breaker on critical-path dependencies

statements.applies_when: the content creates or configures a circuit breaker.
statements.not_applies_when: No circuit breaker, bulkhead, concurrency limit or load shedding is configured and no dependency is called.
statements.text: Circuit breaker thresholds (failure rate, slow-call threshold, open duration) MUST be set in configuration with values stated per dependency, not left at library defaults.
statements.title: Breaker thresholds in configuration

statements.applies_when: the content calls a dependency through a circuit breaker or catches its exception.
statements.not_applies_when: No circuit breaker, bulkhead, concurrency limit or load shedding is configured and no dependency is called.
statements.text: Code SHOULD handle the open-breaker exception explicitly, returning a fallback or a 503, instead of letting it surface as a 500.
statements.title: Behavior when open

statements.applies_when: the content configures an HTTP client connection pool, thread pool, executor or semaphore used for calls to a dependency.
statements.not_applies_when: No circuit breaker, bulkhead, concurrency limit or load shedding is configured and no dependency is called.
statements.text: Each remote dependency MUST have its own bounded connection pool or bulkhead, so that one slow dependency cannot use every worker or connection.
statements.title: Separate pools per dependency

statements.applies_when: the content configures server worker counts, request queues, max connections or concurrency limits.
statements.not_applies_when: No circuit breaker, bulkhead, concurrency limit or load shedding is configured and no dependency is called.
statements.text: Services on the booking path SHOULD set a maximum number of in-flight requests and reject excess requests with 503 and `Retry-After` instead of queueing them.
statements.title: Server concurrency limit

statements.applies_when: the content implements load shedding, admission control or request prioritisation.
statements.not_applies_when: No circuit breaker, bulkhead, concurrency limit or load shedding is configured and no dependency is called.
statements.text: When shedding load, a service SHOULD reject background and batch traffic before user-facing traffic, using the `X-Request-Priority` header.
statements.title: Priority shedding

statements.applies_when: the content creates or configures a circuit breaker.
statements.not_applies_when: No circuit breaker, bulkhead, concurrency limit or load shedding is configured and no dependency is called.
statements.text: Every circuit breaker MUST publish its state and its rejected-call count as metrics tagged with the dependency name.
statements.title: Breaker metrics

statements.applies_when: the content combines a retry policy with a circuit breaker on the same call.
statements.not_applies_when: No circuit breaker, bulkhead, concurrency limit or load shedding is configured and no dependency is called.
statements.text: Each retry attempt MUST pass through the circuit breaker so the breaker counts it, and retries MUST stop as soon as the breaker is open.
statements.title: Retries counted by the breaker

statements.applies_when: the content is a design that adds a dependency to search, availability, booking or payment.
statements.not_applies_when: No circuit breaker, bulkhead, concurrency limit or load shedding is configured and no dependency is called.
statements.text: A design that adds a dependency to a critical path MUST state which breaker and bulkhead protect it and what the user sees when the breaker is open.
statements.title: Designs state isolation

statements.applies_when: the content configures a concurrency limit or admission control for a service.
statements.not_applies_when: No circuit breaker, bulkhead, concurrency limit or load shedding is configured and no dependency is called.
statements.text: Services MAY use adaptive concurrency limits (for example the Netflix concurrency-limits library) instead of fixed limits.
statements.title: Adaptive limits

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes a server entry point, a signal handler, or the shutdown hook of a service or consumer.
statements.not_applies_when: No health endpoint, probe, startup code or shutdown handling is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Services MUST handle SIGTERM by stopping new work, finishing in-flight requests and messages, and then exiting before the termination grace period ends.
statements.title: Handle SIGTERM

statements.applies_when: the content implements shutdown logic or a readiness endpoint.
statements.not_applies_when: No health endpoint, probe, startup code or shutdown handling is added, changed or described.
statements.text: On shutdown a service MUST mark its readiness check as failing before it closes its listener, so the load balancer stops sending traffic.
statements.title: Readiness fails first

statements.applies_when: the content implements the shutdown or close path of a Kafka or queue consumer.
statements.not_applies_when: No health endpoint, probe, startup code or shutdown handling is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Kafka consumers MUST commit offsets for fully processed messages and leave the consumer group cleanly during shutdown.
statements.title: Commit offsets on shutdown

statements.applies_when: the content implements a liveness endpoint or configures a `livenessProbe`.
statements.not_applies_when: No health endpoint, probe, startup code or shutdown handling is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Liveness probes MUST check only that the process can serve, and MUST NOT call databases, caches or other services.
statements.title: Liveness checks the process only

statements.applies_when: the content implements a readiness endpoint or adds a check to it.
statements.not_applies_when: No health endpoint, probe, startup code or shutdown handling is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Readiness SHOULD fail when a dependency the service cannot work without (its own database) is unreachable, and SHOULD NOT fail for non-essential dependencies.
statements.title: Readiness checks hard dependencies

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes a health, liveness or readiness route, or the probe paths in a manifest.
statements.not_applies_when: No health endpoint, probe, startup code or shutdown handling is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Health endpoints MUST be served at `/health/live` and `/health/ready` on the management port.
statements.title: Health endpoint paths

statements.applies_when: the content configures `startupProbe`, `initialDelaySeconds` or other probe timings.
statements.not_applies_when: No health endpoint, probe, startup code or shutdown handling is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Services that need more than 10 seconds to start SHOULD use a startup probe instead of a long initial delay on the liveness probe.
statements.title: Startup probe for slow starts

statements.applies_when: the content reads environment variables or configuration files at service startup.
statements.not_applies_when: No health endpoint, probe, startup code or shutdown handling is added, changed or described.
statements.text: A service MUST validate its mandatory configuration at startup and exit with a non-zero code and a clear message when a value is missing or invalid.
statements.title: Fail fast on bad configuration

statements.applies_when: the content adds startup logic that loads caches, opens connection pools or pre-computes data.
statements.not_applies_when: No health endpoint, probe, startup code or shutdown handling is added, changed or described.
statements.text: JVM and other services with cold-start latency SHOULD warm up caches and connection pools before reporting ready.
statements.title: Warm-up before ready

statements.applies_when: the content configures a `preStop` hook or `terminationGracePeriodSeconds`.
statements.not_applies_when: No health endpoint, probe, startup code or shutdown handling is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Deployments MAY add a short `preStop` sleep of 5 to 10 seconds to cover load balancer propagation delay.
statements.title: Pre-stop delay

statements.applies_when: the content adds a SELECT, `findAll`, `.all()`, `objects.filter` or repository method whose result is returned or iterated.
statements.not_applies_when: No SQL query, ORM query, repository method or index is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Queries that return rows to a request handler MUST have a `LIMIT` or page size, and MUST NOT load an entire table or an unbounded relation.
statements.title: Bounded result sets

statements.applies_when: the content accesses a lazy relation or calls a repository or query method inside a loop over results.
statements.not_applies_when: No SQL query, ORM query, repository method or index is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Code MUST NOT run one query per item of a collection; it has to batch with `IN`, a join or the ORM's eager loading (`select_related`, `prefetch_related`, `JOIN FETCH`, `include`).
statements.title: No N+1 queries

statements.applies_when: the content adds a WHERE clause, ORDER BY or ORM filter on a large table such as reservations, availability, reviews or users.
statements.not_applies_when: No SQL query, ORM query, repository method or index is added, changed or described.
statements.text: A new query that filters or sorts a table with more than one million rows MUST be backed by an index on the filtered columns, added in the same change or already present.
statements.title: Index for new filters

statements.applies_when: the content contains `CREATE INDEX` on an existing table in a migration.
statements.not_applies_when: No SQL query, ORM query, repository method or index is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Indexes on existing PostgreSQL tables MUST be created with `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY`.
statements.title: Concurrent index creation

statements.applies_when: the content writes `SELECT *` or loads full entities only to read one or two fields.
statements.not_applies_when: No SQL query, ORM query, repository method or index is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Queries on wide tables SHOULD select the needed columns instead of `SELECT *` or full entity loads.
statements.title: Select only needed columns

statements.applies_when: the content uses `OFFSET`, `.skip()`, `Pageable` or page-number paging on a large table.
statements.not_applies_when: No SQL query, ORM query, repository method or index is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Endpoints that page through large tables SHOULD use keyset pagination on an indexed column rather than `OFFSET`.
statements.title: Keyset pagination for deep pages

statements.applies_when: the content writes a WHERE clause that applies a function or cast to a column.
statements.not_applies_when: No SQL query, ORM query, repository method or index is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Filters SHOULD NOT wrap an indexed column in a function (`LOWER(email)`, `DATE(created_at)`) unless a matching expression index exists.
statements.title: No functions on indexed columns

statements.applies_when: the content configures a database connection, data source, connection pool or database role.
statements.not_applies_when: No SQL query, ORM query, repository method or index is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Application database users MUST have a `statement_timeout` of at most 5 seconds for request traffic, and batch jobs MUST set their own explicit timeout.
statements.title: Statement timeout

statements.applies_when: the content adds a report, export, aggregation or analytics query in a service.
statements.not_applies_when: No SQL query, ORM query, repository method or index is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Reporting, export and analytics queries MUST run on a read replica or the warehouse, not on the primary.
statements.title: Heavy reads on replicas

statements.applies_when: the content adds a new query on a large table.
statements.not_applies_when: No SQL query, ORM query, repository method or index is added, changed or described.
statements.text: A pull request that adds a query on a large table MAY include the `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` output from staging.
statements.title: Query plans in reviews

statements.applies_when: the content contains `CREATE TABLE` or an ORM model for a new table.
statements.not_applies_when: No table is created, no rows are deleted or archived, and no backup configuration is added, changed or described.
statements.text: A migration that creates a table MUST declare the table's retention period in a table comment or in the service's `data-catalog.yaml`.
statements.title: Retention declared for new tables

statements.applies_when: the content adds a table with a retention period, or adds a job that deletes old rows.
statements.not_applies_when: No table is created, no rows are deleted or archived, and no backup configuration is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Tables with a finite retention MUST have a scheduled purge or archive job that deletes expired rows in batches of at most 10,000 rows.
statements.title: Purge job for time-bound data

statements.applies_when: the content adds a column that marks rows as deleted, archived or inactive.
statements.not_applies_when: No table is created, no rows are deleted or archived, and no backup configuration is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Soft delete SHOULD use a nullable `deleted_at` timestamp rather than a boolean flag.
statements.title: Soft delete column

statements.applies_when: the content queries a table that has a `deleted_at` or `is_deleted` column, or adds such a column.
statements.not_applies_when: No table is created, no rows are deleted or archived, and no backup configuration is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Queries on a soft-deleted table MUST exclude deleted rows by default through a global ORM filter or a view, not by a condition repeated in each query.
statements.title: Soft-deleted rows filtered

statements.applies_when: the content adds a unique constraint or unique index on a table with soft delete.
statements.not_applies_when: No table is created, no rows are deleted or archived, and no backup configuration is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Unique constraints on soft-deleted tables SHOULD be partial indexes that only cover rows where `deleted_at IS NULL`.
statements.title: Unique constraints with soft delete

statements.applies_when: the content issues a DELETE or UPDATE statement or an ORM bulk delete or bulk update.
statements.not_applies_when: No table is created, no rows are deleted or archived, and no backup configuration is added, changed or described.
statements.text: A `DELETE` or `UPDATE` without a `WHERE` clause, or one that can touch more than 10,000 rows, MUST NOT run in a request handler.
statements.title: Bulk deletes guarded

statements.applies_when: the content creates or changes a production database instance, cluster or its backup settings.
statements.not_applies_when: No table is created, no rows are deleted or archived, and no backup configuration is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Production databases MUST have point-in-time recovery enabled with at least 14 days of retention.
statements.title: Point-in-time recovery

statements.applies_when: the content creates a new production database or changes its backup or restore procedure.
statements.not_applies_when: No table is created, no rows are deleted or archived, and no backup configuration is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Each production database SHOULD have a restore test run at least every quarter, with the measured restore time recorded in the service runbook.
statements.title: Restore tested

statements.applies_when: the content implements a purge or archive job for old rows.
statements.not_applies_when: No table is created, no rows are deleted or archived, and no backup configuration is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Rows past their online retention MAY be exported to the data lake in Parquet before they are deleted.
statements.title: Archive to cold storage

statements.applies_when: the content adds an import from another workspace package or from a path containing `/src/` or `/internal/` of another package.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not TypeScript source code.
statements.text: Code MUST import other workspace packages through their public entry point (`@tf/booking-core`), never through deep paths such as `@tf/booking-core/src/internal`.
statements.title: Imports through package entry points

statements.applies_when: the content adds import statements between modules of the same package or between packages.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not TypeScript source code.
statements.text: A change MUST NOT introduce an import cycle between files or packages.
statements.title: No cycles between modules

statements.applies_when: the content uses a postfix `!` on an expression, such as `user!.id` or `map.get(key)!`.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not TypeScript source code.
statements.text: Code MUST NOT use the non-null assertion operator `!` on values that can be null or undefined; it has to narrow the value with a check instead.
statements.title: No non-null assertions

statements.applies_when: the content uses `||` to provide a default for a value that is a number, boolean or string.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not TypeScript source code.
statements.text: Defaults for nullable values SHOULD use `??` rather than `||`, so that `0`, `false` and empty strings are kept.
statements.title: Nullish operators

statements.applies_when: the content declares an `enum` or `const enum`.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not TypeScript source code.
statements.text: New code SHOULD use string literal union types or `as const` objects instead of TypeScript `enum` declarations.
statements.title: Unions instead of enums

statements.applies_when: the content writes a `switch` or if/else chain over a union type, discriminated union or status field.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not TypeScript source code.
statements.text: A `switch` on a union or discriminant MUST end with a `default` branch that assigns the value to `never`, so a new member causes a compile error.
statements.title: Exhaustive switches

statements.applies_when: the content declares types for API payloads, component props or state, or modifies an object or array passed as an argument.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not TypeScript source code.
statements.text: Types for API responses, props and store state SHOULD be declared `readonly` or `Readonly<>`, and code SHOULD NOT mutate function arguments.
statements.title: Readonly data

statements.applies_when: the content casts the result of `response.json()`, `JSON.parse`, `localStorage.getItem` or URL search params with `as` or assigns it to a typed variable.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not TypeScript source code.
statements.text: Data parsed from `fetch`, `localStorage`, `postMessage` or URL parameters MUST be validated with a schema (zod) before being used as a typed value, not cast with `as`.
statements.title: Runtime validation of external data

statements.applies_when: the content imports an interface or type alias that is used only in type positions.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not TypeScript source code.
statements.text: Imports used only as types MUST use `import type`.
statements.title: Type-only imports

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes an `index.ts` file that only re-exports other modules.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not TypeScript source code.
statements.text: A package MAY expose a single `index.ts` barrel file at its root as its public entry point.
statements.title: Barrel files

statements.applies_when: the content calls `requests.`, `time.sleep`, `psycopg2`, `urllib` or other synchronous I/O inside an `async def` function.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not Python source code or a Python project file.
statements.text: An `async def` function MUST NOT call blocking I/O such as `requests`, `time.sleep`, `open()` on network storage or a synchronous database driver; it has to use an async client or `asyncio.to_thread`.
statements.title: No blocking calls in async functions

statements.applies_when: the content calls `asyncio.create_task`, `asyncio.ensure_future` or `loop.create_task`.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not Python source code or a Python project file.
statements.text: Every `asyncio.create_task` result MUST be awaited, gathered, or stored in a task group so that its exceptions are not lost.
statements.title: Tasks are awaited or kept

statements.applies_when: the content writes an `except:` clause without an exception type, or catches `BaseException`.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not Python source code or a Python project file.
statements.text: Code MUST NOT use a bare `except:` or `except BaseException:` except at the top level of a process, where it has to re-raise after logging.
statements.title: No bare except

statements.applies_when: the content writes an `except Exception` clause or an except clause whose body is `pass` or `continue`.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not Python source code or a Python project file.
statements.text: `except Exception` blocks MUST either re-raise, or report the error to Sentry and return an explicit failure value; they MUST NOT silently `pass`.
statements.title: Broad exceptions re-raised or reported

statements.applies_when: the content raises a new exception inside an `except` block.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not Python source code or a Python project file.
statements.text: Exceptions raised while handling another exception SHOULD use `raise ... from err` to keep the original cause.
statements.title: Exception chaining

statements.applies_when: the content raises `Exception(...)`, `RuntimeError(...)` or `ValueError(...)` for a business rule violation.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not Python source code or a Python project file.
statements.text: Libraries and services SHOULD define their own exception classes for domain errors instead of raising `Exception` or `ValueError` with a message string.
statements.title: Domain exceptions

statements.applies_when: the content defines a data class, NamedTuple, Pydantic model or passes structured records as dicts.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not Python source code or a Python project file.
statements.text: Value objects and messages SHOULD be `@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)` or Pydantic models with `frozen=True`, rather than plain dicts.
statements.title: Frozen data classes for values

statements.applies_when: the content defines a function parameter or data class field with a list, dict or set default.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not Python source code or a Python project file.
statements.text: Functions and data classes MUST NOT use mutable default values (`[]`, `{}`, `set()`); data classes have to use `field(default_factory=...)`.
statements.title: Mutable defaults

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes `pyproject.toml`, `requirements.txt`, `setup.py` or `setup.cfg`.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not Python source code or a Python project file.
statements.text: Python projects MUST declare dependencies in `pyproject.toml` and commit a `uv.lock`; new projects MUST NOT add `requirements.txt` or `setup.py`.
statements.title: Project managed with uv

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes `requires-python` or the Python version of a project, Dockerfile or CI job.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not Python source code or a Python project file.
statements.text: Projects MUST declare `requires-python` with a supported minor version (3.11 or later).
statements.title: Python version

statements.applies_when: the content runs several coroutines concurrently with `asyncio.gather` or `asyncio.wait`.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not Python source code or a Python project file.
statements.text: New async code MAY use `asyncio.TaskGroup` in place of `asyncio.gather` for groups of related tasks.
statements.title: Structured concurrency

statements.applies_when: the content sets the image tag, artifact version or release identifier used by a deployment.
statements.not_applies_when: No deployment, rollout, release or rollback process is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Each release MUST deploy an immutable artifact identified by a git SHA or semantic version, never a mutable tag such as `latest`.
statements.title: Immutable release artifacts

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes an Argo Rollout, deployment strategy or pipeline stage for a user-facing service.
statements.not_applies_when: No deployment, rollout, release or rollback process is added, changed or described.
statements.text: User-facing backend services MUST roll out through a canary step that sends at most 10% of traffic to the new version before full promotion.
statements.title: Canary for user-facing services

statements.applies_when: the content configures a canary step, `AnalysisTemplate`, promotion rule or deployment gate.
statements.not_applies_when: No deployment, rollout, release or rollback process is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Canary promotion MUST be gated on automated analysis of error rate and p99 latency against the stable version, with automatic abort on failure.
statements.title: Automated canary analysis

statements.applies_when: the content changes a deployment pipeline, release script or the rollback procedure of a service.
statements.not_applies_when: No deployment, rollout, release or rollback process is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Every service MUST be able to roll back to the previous release with a single pipeline action, without a code change or manual database work.
statements.title: One-step rollback

statements.applies_when: the content changes the format of a Kafka message, cached value, file or stored payload.
statements.not_applies_when: No deployment, rollout, release or rollback process is added, changed or described.
statements.text: A release that changes a message format, cache format or stored data SHOULD state in the pull request whether the previous version can still read the new data after rollback.
statements.title: Rollback compatibility

statements.applies_when: the content changes deploy schedules, freeze rules, deploy gates or the release calendar.
statements.not_applies_when: No deployment, rollout, release or rollback process is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Production deploys MUST NOT run during a freeze window from the release calendar unless an exception is approved by the on-call engineering manager.
statements.title: Deploy freeze

statements.applies_when: the content describes the rollout timing of a release or configures deploy windows.
statements.not_applies_when: No deployment, rollout, release or rollback process is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Risky changes SHOULD NOT be deployed on Friday after 15:00 local time or on the evening before a public holiday in a main market.
statements.title: Friday evening deploys

statements.applies_when: the content configures the release of an Android or iOS app, Fastlane lanes or store rollout settings.
statements.not_applies_when: No deployment, rollout, release or rollback process is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Mobile app releases SHOULD use staged rollout on Google Play and phased release on the App Store, pausing when the crash-free rate drops below 99.5%.
statements.title: Mobile staged rollout

statements.applies_when: the content changes release tooling, changelog generation or deploy notifications.
statements.not_applies_when: No deployment, rollout, release or rollback process is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Each production release MUST have release notes generated from merged pull requests and linked from the deploy event.
statements.title: Release notes

statements.applies_when: the content configures a promotion step or approval gate in a deployment pipeline.
statements.not_applies_when: No deployment, rollout, release or rollback process is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Teams MAY require a manual approval step before full promotion for services that handle payments.
statements.title: Manual promotion

statements.applies_when: the content proposes introducing a technology, datastore, broker, framework or managed cloud service not already used by the organisation.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is code, a diff, an incident report, or a document that neither records an architecture decision nor proposes a system design.
statements.text: Adopting a new language, datastore, message broker, framework or cloud service MUST be recorded in an ADR in the `architecture-decisions` repository.
statements.title: ADR for lasting technology choices

statements.applies_when: the content is an architecture decision record.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is code, a diff, an incident report, or a document that neither records an architecture decision nor proposes a system design.
statements.text: An ADR MUST contain the sections Status, Context, Decision, Consequences and Options Considered.
statements.title: ADR structure

statements.applies_when: the content is an architecture decision record or changes its status.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is code, a diff, an incident report, or a document that neither records an architecture decision nor proposes a system design.
statements.text: An ADR's status MUST be one of Proposed, Accepted, Rejected or Superseded, and a superseded ADR MUST link to the ADR that replaces it.
statements.title: ADR status values

statements.applies_when: the content edits the Decision or Context section of an ADR with status Accepted.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is code, a diff, an incident report, or a document that neither records an architecture decision nor proposes a system design.
statements.text: An accepted ADR SHOULD NOT be rewritten; a changed decision SHOULD be recorded as a new ADR that supersedes it.
statements.title: ADRs are immutable

statements.applies_when: the content is a design that adds a service, endpoint, consumer or job.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is code, a diff, an incident report, or a document that neither records an architecture decision nor proposes a system design.
statements.text: A design that adds a service or endpoint MUST estimate peak requests per second, including the Friday dinner peak and expected growth over 18 months.
statements.title: Traffic estimate

statements.applies_when: the content is a design that adds a database, table, bucket, index or topic.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is code, a diff, an incident report, or a document that neither records an architecture decision nor proposes a system design.
statements.text: A design that adds a datastore or table MUST estimate row count or data size after one and three years, and the growth rate.
statements.title: Storage estimate

statements.applies_when: the content is a design that adds cloud resources, a managed service, a third-party vendor or significant traffic.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is code, a diff, an incident report, or a document that neither records an architecture decision nor proposes a system design.
statements.text: A design SHOULD include the expected monthly infrastructure cost and the main cost driver.
statements.title: Cost estimate

statements.applies_when: the content is a design that states or implies expected load, throughput or data volume.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is code, a diff, an incident report, or a document that neither records an architecture decision nor proposes a system design.
statements.text: A design SHOULD name the first component that saturates as load grows and the load at which it does.
statements.title: Scaling limit

statements.applies_when: the content is a design for a component used in search, availability, booking or payment.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is code, a diff, an incident report, or a document that neither records an architecture decision nor proposes a system design.
statements.text: A design for a component on the booking path MUST include a load test plan with a target of at least twice the estimated peak.
statements.title: Load test plan

statements.applies_when: the content records a decision that affects only one team's services.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is code, a diff, an incident report, or a document that neither records an architecture decision nor proposes a system design.
statements.text: Small team-local decisions MAY be recorded as a short ADR in the service repository's `docs/adr` folder instead of the central repository.
statements.title: Lightweight ADRs

statements.applies_when: the content builds a cache key or key prefix for Redis, Memcached or an in-memory cache.
statements.not_applies_when: No cache is read, written or configured and no HTTP caching header is set.
statements.text: Cache keys MUST start with the service name and a schema version, for example `availability:v3:{restaurantId}:{date}`.
statements.title: Namespaced, versioned keys

statements.applies_when: the content writes to a cache (`set`, `put`, `SETEX`, `@Cacheable`) or creates an in-memory cache (Caffeine, `lru-cache`, `functools.lru_cache`).
statements.not_applies_when: No cache is read, written or configured and no HTTP caching header is set.
statements.text: Every cache write MUST set a TTL, and in-memory caches MUST have a maximum size.
statements.title: Every entry expires

statements.applies_when: the content caches a response or object that contains user profile, booking, payment or other per-user data.
statements.not_applies_when: No cache is read, written or configured and no HTTP caching header is set.
statements.text: Responses that contain user-specific or personal data MUST include the user id in the cache key, or MUST NOT be cached in a shared cache.
statements.title: Personal data keyed by user

statements.applies_when: the content updates or deletes a database record that is also stored in a cache.
statements.not_applies_when: No cache is read, written or configured and no HTTP caching header is set.
statements.text: Code that updates a record served from cache MUST delete or update the cache entry after the database commit, not before it.
statements.title: Invalidation on write

statements.applies_when: the content implements a cache-aside read for data requested by many clients, such as restaurant pages, menus or search results.
statements.not_applies_when: No cache is read, written or configured and no HTTP caching header is set.
statements.text: Hot keys SHOULD be protected against stampedes with request coalescing, a lock, or early probabilistic refresh.
statements.title: Stampede protection

statements.applies_when: the content sets TTLs for many keys in a loop, a warm-up job or a bulk cache fill.
statements.not_applies_when: No cache is read, written or configured and no HTTP caching header is set.
statements.text: TTLs for large batches of keys written at the same time SHOULD include random jitter of about 10% so they do not expire together.
statements.title: TTL jitter

statements.applies_when: the content calls a Redis or Memcached client on a request path or handles its errors.
statements.not_applies_when: No cache is read, written or configured and no HTTP caching header is set.
statements.text: A cache read or write error MUST be treated as a cache miss and MUST NOT fail the request.
statements.title: Cache failure is not request failure

statements.applies_when: the content sets response headers, adds an endpoint that returns data to browsers or apps, or configures CDN caching rules.
statements.not_applies_when: No cache is read, written or configured and no HTTP caching header is set.
statements.text: HTTP responses from public APIs and web pages MUST set an explicit `Cache-Control` header; authenticated responses MUST use `private` or `no-store`.
statements.title: Explicit Cache-Control

statements.applies_when: the content returns localized or content-negotiated responses that pass through a CDN or shared cache.
statements.not_applies_when: No cache is read, written or configured and no HTTP caching header is set.
statements.text: Responses cached by a CDN that change with `Accept-Language` or `Accept-Encoding` MUST declare those headers in `Vary` or include them in the CDN cache key.
statements.title: Vary on content negotiation

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes a GET endpoint for menus, photos, restaurant details or configuration.
statements.not_applies_when: No cache is read, written or configured and no HTTP caching header is set.
statements.text: Endpoints returning large, rarely changing resources SHOULD support `ETag` and `If-None-Match` so clients receive 304 responses.
statements.title: ETags on large resources

statements.applies_when: the content configures CDN caching or `Cache-Control` for public pages.
statements.not_applies_when: No cache is read, written or configured and no HTTP caching header is set.
statements.text: CDN rules MAY use `stale-while-revalidate` for restaurant pages and search results to hide origin latency.
statements.title: Stale while revalidate

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes a `containers:` or `initContainers:` entry in a Deployment, StatefulSet, DaemonSet, Job or CronJob pod template, or the Helm values that fill its `resources` block.
statements.not_applies_when: No Kubernetes workload, pod template or the Helm values feeding one is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Every container and init container in a pod template MUST declare `resources.requests.cpu` and `resources.requests.memory`.
statements.title: CPU and memory requests on every container

statements.applies_when: the content sets or changes `resources.limits.memory` or `resources.requests.memory` on a container.
statements.not_applies_when: No Kubernetes workload, pod template or the Helm values feeding one is added, changed or described.
statements.text: The memory limit of a container MUST be set and MUST be equal to its memory request, so the pod is never killed for memory that the scheduler did not reserve.
statements.title: Memory limit equal to memory request

statements.applies_when: the content sets `resources.limits.cpu` on a container of an HTTP or gRPC service that serves requests.
statements.not_applies_when: No Kubernetes workload, pod template or the Helm values feeding one is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Containers that serve synchronous user traffic SHOULD NOT set a CPU limit, because CFS throttling adds tail latency; they rely on the CPU request for fair sharing instead.
statements.title: No CPU limit on latency-sensitive services

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes a container exposed by a Kubernetes Service, or its `readinessProbe`.
statements.not_applies_when: No Kubernetes workload, pod template or the Helm values feeding one is added, changed or described.
statements.text: A container that receives traffic through a Service MUST define a `readinessProbe` that checks the container's own ability to serve and does not call downstream dependencies.
statements.title: Readiness probe on serving containers

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes a `livenessProbe` on a container.
statements.not_applies_when: No Kubernetes workload, pod template or the Helm values feeding one is added, changed or described.
statements.text: A `livenessProbe` MUST NOT check databases, brokers or other services, and its `failureThreshold` times `periodSeconds` MUST be longer than the worst expected garbage collection or startup pause.
statements.title: Liveness probe independent of dependencies

statements.applies_when: the content sets `initialDelaySeconds` above 30 on a probe, or adds a probe to a JVM or other slow-starting container.
statements.not_applies_when: No Kubernetes workload, pod template or the Helm values feeding one is added, changed or described.
statements.text: A container that takes more than 30 seconds to become ready, such as a JVM service, SHOULD use a `startupProbe` instead of a long `initialDelaySeconds` on the liveness probe.
statements.title: Startup probe for slow-starting containers

statements.applies_when: the content sets `replicas`, `minReplicas` or the Helm value for replica count of a production service.
statements.not_applies_when: No Kubernetes workload, pod template or the Helm values feeding one is added, changed or described.
statements.text: A production Deployment serving user traffic MUST run at least two replicas, set either by `replicas` or by the `minReplicas` of its HorizontalPodAutoscaler.
statements.title: At least two replicas in production

statements.applies_when: the content adds a production Deployment or StatefulSet, or adds or changes a `PodDisruptionBudget`.
statements.not_applies_when: No Kubernetes workload, pod template or the Helm values feeding one is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Every production Deployment or StatefulSet with more than one replica MUST have a PodDisruptionBudget whose `maxUnavailable` or `minAvailable` still lets a node drain evict at least one pod.
statements.title: PodDisruptionBudget for multi-replica workloads

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes the pod template spec of a production Deployment with two or more replicas.
statements.not_applies_when: No Kubernetes workload, pod template or the Helm values feeding one is added, changed or described.
statements.text: A production Deployment SHOULD declare `topologySpreadConstraints` on `topology.kubernetes.io/zone` so that the loss of one availability zone does not remove all replicas.
statements.title: Spread replicas across zones

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes `securityContext`, `privileged`, `hostNetwork`, `hostPID` or `capabilities` in a pod template or container.
statements.not_applies_when: No Kubernetes workload, pod template or the Helm values feeding one is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Pod templates MUST set `runAsNonRoot: true`, `allowPrivilegeEscalation: false`, drop all Linux capabilities and MUST NOT set `privileged: true` or `hostNetwork: true`.
statements.title: Restricted pod security context

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes a container `securityContext` or its `volumeMounts`.
statements.not_applies_when: No Kubernetes workload, pod template or the Helm values feeding one is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Containers MAY set `readOnlyRootFilesystem: true` and mount an `emptyDir` for the paths they write, and this is the preferred way to satisfy the security context when the application allows it.
statements.title: Read-only root filesystem

statements.applies_when: the content adds a new `Chart.yaml`, or adds templates for Deployment, Service or HorizontalPodAutoscaler to a service chart.
statements.not_applies_when: No Helm chart, values file, CronJob, Job, ConfigMap or Kubernetes configuration reference is added, changed or described.
statements.text: A new service chart MUST declare the shared `service` library chart as a dependency and MUST NOT copy its Deployment, Service or HPA templates into the service chart.
statements.title: Use the shared library chart

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes a Helm values file, or a template that tests `.Values.env`, `.Release.Namespace` or a similar environment name.
statements.not_applies_when: No Helm chart, values file, CronJob, Job, ConfigMap or Kubernetes configuration reference is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Environment differences MUST live in `values-<env>.yaml` files on top of a common `values.yaml`, and templates MUST NOT branch on the environment name.
statements.title: One values file per environment

statements.applies_when: the content sets `image.tag`, `image.repository` or an `image:` field in a values file or manifest.
statements.not_applies_when: No Helm chart, values file, CronJob, Job, ConfigMap or Kubernetes configuration reference is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Image references in values files MUST pin a version tag or digest produced by CI and MUST NOT use `latest` or a branch name as the tag.
statements.title: Immutable image references

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes `metadata.labels` in a Helm template or manifest.
statements.not_applies_when: No Helm chart, values file, CronJob, Job, ConfigMap or Kubernetes configuration reference is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Every rendered object SHOULD carry the labels `app.kubernetes.io/name`, `app.kubernetes.io/version`, `team` and `tier`, set from the library chart helpers rather than written by hand.
statements.title: Standard labels

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes a Kubernetes `CronJob` manifest or its Helm values.
statements.not_applies_when: No Helm chart, values file, CronJob, Job, ConfigMap or Kubernetes configuration reference is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Every CronJob MUST set `concurrencyPolicy` explicitly, and it MUST be `Forbid` unless the job is documented as safe to run in parallel with itself.
statements.title: CronJob concurrency policy

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes a Kubernetes `CronJob` or the `jobTemplate` of one.
statements.not_applies_when: No Helm chart, values file, CronJob, Job, ConfigMap or Kubernetes configuration reference is added, changed or described.
statements.text: A CronJob MUST set `startingDeadlineSeconds`, `activeDeadlineSeconds` on its job template and bounded `successfulJobsHistoryLimit` and `failedJobsHistoryLimit`.
statements.title: CronJob deadlines and history

statements.applies_when: the content sets or changes the `schedule` field of a CronJob.
statements.not_applies_when: No Helm chart, values file, CronJob, Job, ConfigMap or Kubernetes configuration reference is added, changed or described.
statements.text: A CronJob schedule SHOULD set `timeZone` explicitly instead of relying on the controller's default UTC, when the schedule is tied to restaurant opening hours or local business time.
statements.title: Explicit CronJob time zone

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes a Kubernetes `Job` or the `jobTemplate` of a `CronJob`.
statements.not_applies_when: No Helm chart, values file, CronJob, Job, ConfigMap or Kubernetes configuration reference is added, changed or described.
statements.text: A Job or CronJob job template MUST set `backoffLimit` to a value of 3 or less, so a failing job does not create pods indefinitely.
statements.title: Job retry limit

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes a ConfigMap consumed by a Deployment, or the pod template annotations of that Deployment.
statements.not_applies_when: No Helm chart, values file, CronJob, Job, ConfigMap or Kubernetes configuration reference is added, changed or described.
statements.text: A Deployment that reads a ConfigMap SHOULD carry a pod template annotation with the checksum of that ConfigMap, so that a configuration change triggers a rollout.
statements.title: Roll pods when configuration changes

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes the `data` of a ConfigMap or the Helm values rendered into one.
