statements.not_applies_when: No Helm chart, values file, CronJob, Job, ConfigMap or Kubernetes configuration reference is added, changed or described.
statements.text: A ConfigMap MUST NOT contain passwords, tokens or connection strings with credentials; those values come from an ExternalSecret synced from the secret manager.
statements.title: No sensitive values in ConfigMaps

statements.applies_when: the content changes files under a Helm chart's `templates/` directory or its `values.yaml`.
statements.not_applies_when: No Helm chart, values file, CronJob, Job, ConfigMap or Kubernetes configuration reference is added, changed or described.
statements.text: A change to a chart's templates or default values MAY skip the `version` bump in `Chart.yaml` only when the chart is not published to the chart repository.
statements.title: Chart version bump

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes a `backend` block, a `terraform { }` block of a root stack, or adds a `.tfstate` file.
statements.not_applies_when: No Terraform file, module, backend, provider or resource tag is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Every root stack MUST use the shared S3 backend with DynamoDB locking and encryption enabled, and MUST NOT use local state or commit `.tfstate` files.
statements.title: Remote locked state

statements.applies_when: the content adds a root stack or adds resources for another environment to an existing stack.
statements.not_applies_when: No Terraform file, module, backend, provider or resource tag is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Production and non-production resources MUST live in separate root stacks with separate state files; a single state MUST NOT span environments.
statements.title: One state per environment

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes a `required_providers` block or a `provider` block.
statements.not_applies_when: No Terraform file, module, backend, provider or resource tag is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Every root stack and module MUST pin each provider in `required_providers` with a pessimistic constraint such as `~> 5.40`, and the `.terraform.lock.hcl` file MUST be committed.
statements.title: Pinned provider versions

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes a `module` block's `source` or `version`.
statements.not_applies_when: No Terraform file, module, backend, provider or resource tag is added, changed or described.
statements.text: A module sourced from `infra-modules` or a public registry MUST reference an immutable tag or version, never a branch or an unversioned Git reference.
statements.title: Pinned module sources

statements.applies_when: the content adds a taggable cloud resource, or changes `tags` or `default_tags`.
statements.not_applies_when: No Terraform file, module, backend, provider or resource tag is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Every taggable resource MUST carry the tags `team`, `service`, `environment` and `cost-center`, preferably through the provider `default_tags` block.
statements.title: Mandatory tags

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes a database, storage bucket, KMS key or DNS zone resource in a production stack.
statements.not_applies_when: No Terraform file, module, backend, provider or resource tag is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Databases, buckets with data, KMS keys and DNS zones MUST set `lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true }` in production stacks.
statements.title: Protect stateful resources

statements.applies_when: the content renames a resource or module block, or moves resources between modules.
statements.not_applies_when: No Terraform file, module, backend, provider or resource tag is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Renaming or moving a resource address SHOULD use a `moved` block instead of `terraform state mv` run by hand, so the refactor is reviewed and reproducible.
statements.title: Refactor with moved blocks

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes a `variable` block in a Terraform module.
statements.not_applies_when: No Terraform file, module, backend, provider or resource tag is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Every module input variable SHOULD declare a `type` and a `description`, and use a `validation` block when only some values are valid.
statements.title: Typed and documented module variables

statements.applies_when: the content describes or scripts how Terraform changes are applied, or changes the Terraform CI workflow.
statements.not_applies_when: No Terraform file, module, backend, provider or resource tag is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Changes to production stacks MUST be applied only by the CI pipeline from the plan attached to the merged pull request, never by `terraform apply` from a laptop.
statements.title: Plan reviewed before apply

statements.applies_when: the content adds a literal account id, VPC id, subnet id or ARN to Terraform code.
statements.not_applies_when: No Terraform file, module, backend, provider or resource tag is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Modules MAY hard-code account, VPC or subnet identifiers only in root stacks; inside a reusable module those values come from variables or data sources.
statements.title: Data sources over hard-coded identifiers

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes an `aws_s3_bucket`, `google_storage_bucket` or its public access block.
statements.not_applies_when: No storage bucket, managed database or their encryption, backup or access configuration is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Every S3 bucket MUST have an `aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block` with all four settings set to `true`, unless it is a static asset origin served only through the CDN.
statements.title: Block public access on buckets

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes a bucket policy, a bucket ACL or an IAM binding on a bucket.
statements.not_applies_when: No storage bucket, managed database or their encryption, backup or access configuration is added, changed or described.
statements.text: A bucket policy or ACL MUST NOT grant access to `*`, `AllUsers` or `allAuthenticatedUsers`.
statements.title: No public ACLs or wildcard bucket policies

statements.applies_when: the content adds a bucket or database resource, or changes its `kms_key_id`, `server_side_encryption_configuration` or `storage_encrypted` settings.
statements.not_applies_when: No storage bucket, managed database or their encryption, backup or access configuration is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Buckets and databases that store personal or booking data MUST be encrypted with a customer managed KMS key owned by the service, not only the provider default key.
statements.title: Encryption at rest with managed keys

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes an S3 bucket policy.
statements.not_applies_when: No storage bucket, managed database or their encryption, backup or access configuration is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Bucket policies SHOULD deny requests where `aws:SecureTransport` is `false`.
statements.title: TLS-only access to buckets

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes an S3 or GCS bucket, its versioning or its lifecycle configuration.
statements.not_applies_when: No storage bucket, managed database or their encryption, backup or access configuration is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Buckets that hold data other than temporary files SHOULD enable versioning and SHOULD define a lifecycle rule that expires non-current versions.
statements.title: Versioning and lifecycle on data buckets

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes an RDS, Aurora or Cloud SQL instance or cluster, or its `backup_retention_period` or backup settings.
statements.not_applies_when: No storage bucket, managed database or their encryption, backup or access configuration is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Production relational databases MUST enable automated backups with a retention of at least 14 days and point-in-time recovery.
statements.title: Automated backups with retention

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes a production database resource or its `deletion_protection` or `skip_final_snapshot` attributes.
statements.not_applies_when: No storage bucket, managed database or their encryption, backup or access configuration is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Production databases MUST set `deletion_protection = true` and MUST NOT set `skip_final_snapshot = true`.
statements.title: Deletion protection and final snapshot

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes a database or cache resource, its subnet group or its `publicly_accessible` attribute.
statements.not_applies_when: No storage bucket, managed database or their encryption, backup or access configuration is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Databases and caches MUST be placed in private subnets and MUST set `publicly_accessible = false`.
statements.title: Databases in private subnets only

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes a production database instance or cluster, or its `multi_az` or replica settings.
statements.not_applies_when: No storage bucket, managed database or their encryption, backup or access configuration is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Production databases that serve the booking flow SHOULD run Multi-AZ or with a replica in a second zone.
statements.title: Multi-AZ for production databases

statements.applies_when: the content is a design that adds a new database, bucket or other datastore.
statements.not_applies_when: No storage bucket, managed database or their encryption, backup or access configuration is added, changed or described.
statements.text: A design that introduces a new production datastore MUST state its backup schedule, retention, recovery point objective and how a restore is tested.
statements.title: Restore tested in designs

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes a bucket that stores data exports, or its logging configuration.
statements.not_applies_when: No storage bucket, managed database or their encryption, backup or access configuration is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Buckets holding exports of personal data MAY forward access logs to the central logging bucket instead of enabling server access logging on each bucket.
statements.title: Access logging on sensitive buckets

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes an IAM policy document, `aws_iam_policy`, `aws_iam_role_policy` or `jsonencode` policy block.
statements.not_applies_when: No IAM role, policy, service account or network exposure setting is added, changed or described.
statements.text: An IAM policy statement with `Effect = "Allow"` MUST NOT combine `Action = "*"` or a service wildcard like `s3:*` with `Resource = "*"`.
statements.title: No wildcard actions and resources

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes the `Resource` or `Condition` of an IAM policy statement.
statements.not_applies_when: No IAM role, policy, service account or network exposure setting is added, changed or described.
statements.text: IAM statements SHOULD name the specific ARNs the workload uses instead of `*`, and SHOULD use conditions such as `aws:ResourceTag` when the ARNs are not known in advance.
statements.title: Resource-scoped permissions

statements.applies_when: the content adds an `aws_iam_access_key`, a `google_service_account_key`, or an IAM role for a Kubernetes service account.
statements.not_applies_when: No IAM role, policy, service account or network exposure setting is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Workloads on Kubernetes MUST obtain cloud credentials through IRSA or Workload Identity and MUST NOT use `aws_iam_access_key` or exported service account key files.
statements.title: Workload identity instead of static keys

statements.applies_when: the content adds an IAM role or service account, or attaches an existing role to a new workload.
statements.not_applies_when: No IAM role, policy, service account or network exposure setting is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Each service MUST have its own IAM role or service account; roles MUST NOT be shared between services.
statements.title: One role per service

statements.applies_when: the content attaches a managed policy or predefined role to an IAM role, user, group or service account.
statements.not_applies_when: No IAM role, policy, service account or network exposure setting is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Workload roles MUST NOT attach `AdministratorAccess`, `PowerUserAccess` or the `roles/owner` and `roles/editor` roles.
statements.title: No managed admin policies on workloads

statements.applies_when: the content adds an `aws_iam_user`, a user policy attachment, or an IAM binding for an individual `user:` member.
statements.not_applies_when: No IAM role, policy, service account or network exposure setting is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Permissions for people SHOULD be granted to SSO permission sets or groups, not to individual IAM users.
statements.title: Human access through groups and SSO

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes an ingress rule, `aws_security_group_rule`, `aws_vpc_security_group_ingress_rule` or `google_compute_firewall`.
statements.not_applies_when: No IAM role, policy, service account or network exposure setting is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Security group and firewall ingress rules MUST NOT allow `0.0.0.0/0` or `::/0` except on ports 80 and 443 of a public load balancer.
statements.title: No open ingress except public load balancers

statements.applies_when: the content opens port 22, 3389, 5432, 3306, 6379 or 9092 in a security group or firewall rule.
statements.not_applies_when: No IAM role, policy, service account or network exposure setting is added, changed or described.
statements.text: SSH, RDP and database ports MUST NOT be reachable from outside the VPC; access goes through the bastion-less session manager.
statements.title: No administrative ports from the internet

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes a load balancer, its `internal` or `scheme` attribute, or assigns a public IP to an instance.
statements.not_applies_when: No IAM role, policy, service account or network exposure setting is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Services that are only called by other services SHOULD use internal load balancers and SHOULD NOT receive a public IP address.
statements.title: Internal services behind internal load balancers

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes an IAM role `assume_role_policy` that trusts another AWS account or a third-party principal.
statements.not_applies_when: No IAM role, policy, service account or network exposure setting is added, changed or described.
statements.text: A role trust policy that allows another account or a third party MAY omit an `sts:ExternalId` condition only when the trusted principal is an account owned by the company.
statements.title: Cross-account trust scoped by external id

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes a `uses:` line that references an action outside the organisation.
statements.not_applies_when: No GitHub Actions workflow, composite action or reusable workflow is added or changed.
statements.text: Actions from outside the `example-org` organisation MUST be referenced by a full 40-character commit SHA, with the version in a trailing comment.
statements.title: Pin third-party actions to a commit SHA

statements.applies_when: the content adds a workflow file, or changes a `permissions:` block at workflow or job level.
statements.not_applies_when: No GitHub Actions workflow, composite action or reusable workflow is added or changed.
statements.text: Every workflow MUST declare a top-level `permissions:` block, set to `contents: read` or less, and grant wider scopes only on the jobs that need them.
statements.title: Explicit minimal token permissions

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes a workflow with `pull_request_target` or `workflow_run` triggers, or an `actions/checkout` step with a `ref` from the pull request.
statements.not_applies_when: No GitHub Actions workflow, composite action or reusable workflow is added or changed.
statements.text: Workflows triggered by `pull_request_target` or `workflow_run` MUST NOT check out and run code from the pull request head while secrets or a write token are available.
statements.title: No secrets for fork pull requests

statements.applies_when: the content adds a `run:` step that contains `${{ github.event.` or `${{ github.head_ref }}`.
statements.not_applies_when: No GitHub Actions workflow, composite action or reusable workflow is added or changed.
statements.text: Values from `github.event` such as titles, branch names, bodies and commit messages MUST NOT be interpolated with `${{ }}` directly inside a `run:` script; they are passed through `env:` and quoted.
statements.title: No untrusted input in run scripts

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes a workflow step that authenticates to AWS, GCP or another cloud provider.
statements.not_applies_when: No GitHub Actions workflow, composite action or reusable workflow is added or changed.
statements.text: Workflows that deploy or call cloud APIs SHOULD authenticate with OIDC federation (`id-token: write`) instead of long-lived cloud keys stored as repository secrets.
statements.title: Cloud access through OIDC

statements.applies_when: the content adds a job that reads `secrets.` for a deployment, or changes the `environment:` of a job.
statements.not_applies_when: No GitHub Actions workflow, composite action or reusable workflow is added or changed.
statements.text: Deployment secrets SHOULD be defined on a GitHub environment with protection rules, and the job that uses them references that `environment:`.
statements.title: Secrets scoped to environments

statements.applies_when: the content adds a step that uses `secrets.` together with `echo`, `GITHUB_OUTPUT`, `upload-artifact` or `cache`.
statements.not_applies_when: No GitHub Actions workflow, composite action or reusable workflow is added or changed.
statements.text: A workflow step MUST NOT print a secret, write it to `GITHUB_OUTPUT` or `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`, or include it in an uploaded artifact or cache.
statements.title: No secret echo or artifact upload

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes a job in a GitHub Actions workflow.
statements.not_applies_when: No GitHub Actions workflow, composite action or reusable workflow is added or changed.
statements.text: Every job SHOULD set `timeout-minutes` so a hung step does not hold a runner for the default six hours.
statements.title: Job timeouts

statements.applies_when: the content sets `runs-on` to a self-hosted runner label in a workflow triggered by `pull_request`.
statements.not_applies_when: No GitHub Actions workflow, composite action or reusable workflow is added or changed.
statements.text: Jobs on self-hosted runners MUST NOT run for pull requests from forks.
statements.title: Self-hosted runners only for trusted events

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes a `uses:` line that references an action or reusable workflow in the `example-org` organisation.
statements.not_applies_when: No GitHub Actions workflow, composite action or reusable workflow is added or changed.
statements.text: Actions and reusable workflows owned by the organisation MAY be referenced by a release tag instead of a commit SHA.
statements.title: Organisation actions by tag

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes a deploy job, its `needs:` list or its `if:` condition.
statements.not_applies_when: No build, test, publish, deploy or cache step of a CI/CD pipeline is added, changed or described.
statements.text: A deploy job MUST depend through `needs:` on the unit and integration test jobs of the same commit, and MUST NOT run when those jobs fail or are skipped.
statements.title: Tests gate the deploy job

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes `continue-on-error` on a test, lint or scan step or job.
statements.not_applies_when: No build, test, publish, deploy or cache step of a CI/CD pipeline is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Test, lint and security scan steps that gate a deploy MUST NOT set `continue-on-error: true`.
statements.title: No continue-on-error in gating jobs

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes a job that builds, tags or deploys an image or package for staging or production.
statements.not_applies_when: No build, test, publish, deploy or cache step of a CI/CD pipeline is added, changed or described.
statements.text: The image or package deployed to production MUST be the same artifact, identified by digest, that was deployed to staging; production jobs MUST NOT rebuild it.
statements.title: Build once, promote the same artifact

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes a job that pushes an image or package to the release registry.
statements.not_applies_when: No build, test, publish, deploy or cache step of a CI/CD pipeline is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Release images SHOULD be signed with cosign and carry a SLSA provenance attestation generated in the build job.
statements.title: Signed provenance for release artifacts

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes the tags of an image built or pushed by CI.
statements.not_applies_when: No build, test, publish, deploy or cache step of a CI/CD pipeline is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Every published image MUST be tagged with the full Git commit SHA it was built from.
statements.title: Artifact tagged with commit SHA

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes a production deploy job or its `environment:`.
statements.not_applies_when: No build, test, publish, deploy or cache step of a CI/CD pipeline is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Production deploy jobs MUST target a GitHub environment that requires approval from a member of the owning team, except for services enrolled in continuous deployment with automated canary analysis.
statements.title: Manual approval for production

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes an `actions/cache` step, a `cache:` input of a setup action, or a Gradle or Docker layer cache configuration.
statements.not_applies_when: No build, test, publish, deploy or cache step of a CI/CD pipeline is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Dependency caches SHOULD be keyed on the hash of the lock file and the runtime version, and SHOULD NOT cache build outputs between branches.
statements.title: Cache keys from lock files

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes cache `restore-keys` or cache scope in a workflow that builds release artifacts.
statements.not_applies_when: No build, test, publish, deploy or cache step of a CI/CD pipeline is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Release builds on the default branch MUST NOT restore caches written by pull request workflows.
statements.title: No cache restore into release builds from pull requests

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes the steps that run after a deploy job.
statements.not_applies_when: No build, test, publish, deploy or cache step of a CI/CD pipeline is added, changed or described.
statements.text: A deploy pipeline SHOULD run a smoke check against the deployed version and trigger an automatic rollback when it fails.
statements.title: Post-deploy smoke check

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes `paths:` or `paths-ignore:` filters, or a change-detection step in a workflow.
statements.not_applies_when: No build, test, publish, deploy or cache step of a CI/CD pipeline is added, changed or described.
statements.text: In monorepos, build and test jobs MAY use path filters to skip services that did not change, provided that the deploy gate still requires the jobs of every changed service.
statements.title: Path filters for monorepo jobs

statements.applies_when: the content is a design that proposes a new build, release or deployment process.
statements.not_applies_when: No build, test, publish, deploy or cache step of a CI/CD pipeline is added, changed or described.
statements.text: A design that changes how a service is built or deployed MUST describe the pipeline gates, the promotion path between environments and the rollback procedure.
statements.title: Rollout plan in release designs

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes a `FROM` line of the final stage of a Dockerfile.
statements.not_applies_when: No Dockerfile, `.dockerignore` or container image build configuration is added or changed.
statements.text: The final stage of a Dockerfile MUST start `FROM` an image in the internal `registry.internal/base/` catalogue or a distroless image.
statements.title: Approved base images only

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes a `FROM` line in a Dockerfile.
statements.not_applies_when: No Dockerfile, `.dockerignore` or container image build configuration is added or changed.
statements.text: `FROM` lines MUST pin a specific version tag and MUST NOT use `latest`; base image updates arrive through the dependency bot.
statements.title: Pinned base image versions

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes a `USER` instruction or the final stage of a Dockerfile.
statements.not_applies_when: No Dockerfile, `.dockerignore` or container image build configuration is added or changed.
statements.text: The final stage MUST set `USER` to a non-root numeric UID, and MUST NOT switch back to root after that line.
statements.title: Run as a non-root user

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes a Dockerfile that runs a compiler, `npm`, `gradle`, `go build`, `pip install` or similar build step.
statements.not_applies_when: No Dockerfile, `.dockerignore` or container image build configuration is added or changed.
statements.text: Images for compiled languages or bundled frontends MUST use a multi-stage build so compilers, package managers and source code are absent from the final stage.
statements.title: Multi-stage builds for compiled code

statements.applies_when: the content adds `ARG`, `ENV`, `COPY` or `ADD` with names or files such as token, password, key, `.npmrc`, `.netrc` or credentials.
statements.not_applies_when: No Dockerfile, `.dockerignore` or container image build configuration is added or changed.
statements.text: Dockerfiles MUST NOT `COPY` credential files or pass tokens through `ARG` or `ENV`; build-time secrets use `RUN --mount=type=secret`.
statements.title: No secrets in layers or build args

statements.applies_when: the content adds a Dockerfile, a `COPY . .` instruction, or changes `.dockerignore`.
statements.not_applies_when: No Dockerfile, `.dockerignore` or container image build configuration is added or changed.
statements.text: A repository with a Dockerfile SHOULD have a `.dockerignore` that excludes `.git`, `.env` files, local build outputs and test fixtures.
statements.title: Dockerignore excludes local files

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes an `ENTRYPOINT` or `CMD` instruction.
statements.not_applies_when: No Dockerfile, `.dockerignore` or container image build configuration is added or changed.
statements.text: `ENTRYPOINT` and `CMD` SHOULD use the JSON exec form so the process receives `SIGTERM` directly and shuts down gracefully.
statements.title: Exec form for entrypoint

statements.applies_when: the content adds a `RUN` with `apt-get install`, `apk add` or `dnf install`.
statements.not_applies_when: No Dockerfile, `.dockerignore` or container image build configuration is added or changed.
statements.text: A `RUN` that installs OS packages MUST remove the package manager cache in the same instruction and MUST install with `--no-install-recommends` or the equivalent.
statements.title: Clean package manager caches in the same layer

statements.applies_when: the content adds an `ADD` instruction to a Dockerfile.
statements.not_applies_when: No Dockerfile, `.dockerignore` or container image build configuration is added or changed.
statements.text: Dockerfiles SHOULD use `COPY` instead of `ADD` for local files, and download remote files in a `RUN` step that verifies a checksum.
statements.title: COPY instead of ADD

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes `LABEL` instructions or the image labels in a build configuration.
statements.not_applies_when: No Dockerfile, `.dockerignore` or container image build configuration is added or changed.
statements.text: Images MAY carry OCI labels such as `org.opencontainers.image.source` and `org.opencontainers.image.revision` set by CI build arguments.
statements.title: Image metadata labels

statements.applies_when: the content calls `send`, `produce` or `ProducerRecord` with a null, random or constant key, or chooses the key of a new event.
statements.not_applies_when: No Kafka message is produced, no producer or topic is configured and no event schema is added or changed.
statements.text: Every produced message MUST carry a key equal to the identifier of the entity whose events have to stay ordered, such as the reservation id or restaurant id.
statements.title: Key by the entity that needs ordering

statements.applies_when: the content configures a producer value serializer, or publishes a JSON string, map or dictionary to a Kafka topic.
statements.not_applies_when: No Kafka message is produced, no producer or topic is configured and no event schema is added or changed.
statements.text: Values published to a shared topic MUST be serialized with a schema registered in the Schema Registry; producers MUST NOT publish free-form JSON strings.
statements.title: Registered schema for every topic

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes an `.avsc`, `.proto` or JSON Schema file for a Kafka topic, or a generated event class.
statements.not_applies_when: No Kafka message is produced, no producer or topic is configured and no event schema is added or changed.
statements.text: A schema change MUST keep the subject's `BACKWARD_TRANSITIVE` compatibility: new fields have defaults and existing fields are not removed, renamed or retyped.
statements.title: Backward-compatible schema changes

statements.applies_when: the content creates or configures a Kafka producer, or sets `acks`, `enable.idempotence`, `retries` or `max.in.flight.requests.per.connection`.
statements.not_applies_when: No Kafka message is produced, no producer or topic is configured and no event schema is added or changed.
statements.text: Producers MUST set `enable.idempotence=true` and `acks=all`.
statements.title: Idempotent producer

statements.applies_when: the content publishes a Kafka message in the same code path that commits a database transaction.
statements.not_applies_when: No Kafka message is produced, no producer or topic is configured and no event schema is added or changed.
statements.text: An event that reports a database change SHOULD be written through the transactional outbox table instead of publishing to Kafka directly inside the request handler.
statements.title: Outbox for events tied to database writes

statements.applies_when: the content defines a new event type or schema, or builds the payload of a produced message.
statements.not_applies_when: No Kafka message is produced, no producer or topic is configured and no event schema is added or changed.
statements.text: Every event SHOULD carry the envelope fields `event_id`, `event_type`, `occurred_at` in UTC and `producer`, so consumers deduplicate and trace events uniformly.
statements.title: Standard event envelope

statements.applies_when: the content creates a Kafka topic or references a topic name that does not exist yet.
statements.not_applies_when: No Kafka message is produced, no producer or topic is configured and no event schema is added or changed.
statements.text: New topics MUST follow `<domain>.<entity>.<event>.v<major>` and MUST be declared in the topics repository with an owning team, partitions and retention.
statements.title: Topic naming and ownership

statements.applies_when: the content removes, renames or retypes a field of a published event, or changes the meaning of an event.
statements.not_applies_when: No Kafka message is produced, no producer or topic is configured and no event schema is added or changed.
statements.text: A breaking change to an event MUST be published on a new `v<major+1>` topic, with the old topic produced in parallel until its consumers have migrated.
statements.title: New major version for breaking changes

statements.applies_when: the content calls a Kafka producer `send` or `produce` method.
statements.not_applies_when: No Kafka message is produced, no producer or topic is configured and no event schema is added or changed.
statements.text: Code that sends a message MUST handle the failure of the send callback or future and MUST NOT fire and forget.
statements.title: Handle send failures

statements.applies_when: the content configures a producer for a topic, or sets `compression.type`.
statements.not_applies_when: No Kafka message is produced, no producer or topic is configured and no event schema is added or changed.
statements.text: Producers of high-volume topics MAY enable `compression.type=zstd` or `lz4`.
statements.title: Compression

statements.applies_when: the content is a design that proposes publishing a new event or topic.
statements.not_applies_when: No Kafka message is produced, no producer or topic is configured and no event schema is added or changed.
statements.text: A design that adds a new event MUST name the topic, key, schema, expected throughput and the known consumers.
statements.title: Event contracts in designs

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes a Kafka message handler, `@KafkaListener`, consumer loop or `eachMessage` callback that writes state or calls other services.
statements.not_applies_when: No Kafka message is consumed and no consumer, listener or dead-letter topic is configured.
statements.text: A consumer MUST produce the same outcome when it processes the same message twice, for example by recording processed `event_id`s or using conditional writes.
statements.title: Idempotent message handling

statements.applies_when: the content configures `enable.auto.commit`, calls `commitSync`, `commitAsync` or `commitOffsets`, or sets the listener ack mode.
statements.not_applies_when: No Kafka message is consumed and no consumer, listener or dead-letter topic is configured.
statements.text: Offsets MUST be committed only after the message has been fully processed; consumers MUST NOT rely on `enable.auto.commit=true` when processing has side effects.
statements.title: Commit offsets after processing

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes consumer error handling, a retry policy, `DefaultErrorHandler`, `DeadLetterPublishingRecoverer` or a dead-letter topic.
statements.not_applies_when: No Kafka message is consumed and no consumer, listener or dead-letter topic is configured.
statements.text: A message that still fails after a bounded number of retries MUST be published to the consumer's dead-letter topic `<topic>.<consumer-group>.dlt` with the error and original offset in headers.
statements.title: Dead-letter topic after bounded retries

statements.applies_when: the content configures a consumer value deserializer or `ErrorHandlingDeserializer`, or parses message payloads.
statements.not_applies_when: No Kafka message is consumed and no consumer, listener or dead-letter topic is configured.
statements.text: Deserialization failures MUST be caught and routed to the dead-letter topic instead of throwing in a loop on the same offset.
statements.title: Deserialization errors do not block the partition

statements.applies_when: the content adds a sleep, backoff or retry loop inside a Kafka message handler.
statements.not_applies_when: No Kafka message is consumed and no consumer, listener or dead-letter topic is configured.
statements.text: Retries that wait longer than a few seconds SHOULD use retry topics instead of sleeping in the listener thread, so the partition keeps moving and the consumer is not evicted from the group.
statements.title: Non-blocking retries for slow recovery

statements.applies_when: the content sets `max.poll.records`, `max.poll.interval.ms` or changes the batch size of a consumer.
statements.not_applies_when: No Kafka message is consumed and no consumer, listener or dead-letter topic is configured.
statements.text: `max.poll.interval.ms` and `max.poll.records` SHOULD be set so that the worst-case processing time of one batch stays below the poll interval.
statements.title: Poll interval matches processing time

statements.applies_when: the content creates a Kafka consumer or listener, or sets `group.id` or `auto.offset.reset`.
statements.not_applies_when: No Kafka message is consumed and no consumer, listener or dead-letter topic is configured.
statements.text: Each consumer MUST use a dedicated `group.id` named after the service and purpose, and MUST set `auto.offset.reset` explicitly.
statements.title: Explicit consumer group and offset reset

statements.applies_when: the content deserializes or dispatches consumed events by type or maps them to a class.
statements.not_applies_when: No Kafka message is consumed and no consumer, listener or dead-letter topic is configured.
statements.text: Consumers MUST ignore unknown fields and unknown `event_type` values instead of failing, so producers can evolve their schemas.
statements.title: Tolerate unknown fields and event types

statements.applies_when: the content adds a new consumer group, dead-letter topic or its monitoring configuration.
statements.not_applies_when: No Kafka message is consumed and no consumer, listener or dead-letter topic is configured.
statements.text: Every production consumer group SHOULD have an alert on consumer lag and on messages arriving in its dead-letter topic.
statements.title: Lag and dead-letter alerts

statements.applies_when: the content adds code or a job that reads a dead-letter topic and republishes messages.
statements.not_applies_when: No Kafka message is consumed and no consumer, listener or dead-letter topic is configured.
statements.text: Teams MAY replay dead-letter messages with the shared `dlt-replayer` tool instead of writing a custom replay consumer.
statements.title: Replay from the dead-letter topic

statements.applies_when: the content is a design that proposes consuming a Kafka topic or adding an event-driven flow.
statements.not_applies_when: No Kafka message is consumed and no consumer, listener or dead-letter topic is configured.
statements.text: A design that adds a consumer MUST describe its idempotency key, retry policy, dead-letter handling and the effect of replaying the topic from the start.
statements.title: Failure handling in designs

statements.applies_when: the content writes to a warehouse table, data lake path or file from a batch job, Airflow task, dbt model or Spark job.
statements.not_applies_when: No batch job, DAG, dbt model, Spark job or warehouse transformation is added, changed or described.
statements.text: A job MUST produce the same output when it runs twice for the same interval, by overwriting or merging the target partition instead of appending to it.
statements.title: Idempotent writes per partition

statements.applies_when: the content filters data by date or time in a batch job, DAG task, dbt model or Spark job.
statements.not_applies_when: No batch job, DAG, dbt model, Spark job or warehouse transformation is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Jobs MUST derive the processed interval from the scheduler's logical date, such as `data_interval_start` in Airflow, and MUST NOT call `now()` or `CURRENT_DATE` to choose which data to process.
statements.title: Logical date instead of wall clock

statements.applies_when: the content adds a backfill script, sets `catchup`, `max_active_runs`, or describes reprocessing of historical data.
statements.not_applies_when: No batch job, DAG, dbt model, Spark job or warehouse transformation is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Backfills SHOULD run as scheduler runs for past logical dates with bounded concurrency, not as ad-hoc scripts that write to production tables.
statements.title: Backfills through the scheduler

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes a dbt model, a table load consumed by other teams, or its dbt tests or quality checks.
statements.not_applies_when: No batch job, DAG, dbt model, Spark job or warehouse transformation is added, changed or described.
statements.text: A model or table consumed by reports or other teams MUST have checks for primary key uniqueness, non-null keys and row count, and those checks MUST block the downstream publish task when they fail.
statements.title: Data quality checks before publishing

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes a dbt source, an external table, or a sensor waiting for upstream data.
statements.not_applies_when: No batch job, DAG, dbt model, Spark job or warehouse transformation is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Sources that arrive from other systems SHOULD declare a freshness threshold, such as dbt source `freshness`, that alerts when the data is late.
statements.title: Freshness checks on sources

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes an Airflow operator, task or `default_args`.
statements.not_applies_when: No batch job, DAG, dbt model, Spark job or warehouse transformation is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Every Airflow task MUST set `retries`, `retry_delay` and `execution_timeout`.
statements.title: Explicit retries and timeouts on tasks

statements.applies_when: the content schedules a DAG or job relative to another pipeline, or adds an `ExternalTaskSensor` or dataset trigger.
statements.not_applies_when: No batch job, DAG, dbt model, Spark job or warehouse transformation is added, changed or described.
statements.text: A job that depends on another pipeline's output MUST wait on a sensor or dataset event for that output, not on a fixed schedule offset.
statements.title: Dependencies through sensors or datasets

statements.applies_when: the content adds a DAG or changes its `default_args`, `owner` or SLA settings.
statements.not_applies_when: No batch job, DAG, dbt model, Spark job or warehouse transformation is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Every DAG SHOULD set an `owner` that is a team alias and an SLA or deadline alert for its final task.
statements.title: Owner and SLA on DAGs

statements.applies_when: the content reads from or writes to a warehouse table without `ref()` or `source()`, or adds a Spark or Python job that reads or writes tables.
statements.not_applies_when: No batch job, DAG, dbt model, Spark job or warehouse transformation is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Jobs SHOULD emit OpenLineage events or declare dbt `ref`/`source` dependencies so the catalogue shows which tables feed each output.
statements.title: Lineage metadata

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes the `materialized` config of a dbt model.
statements.not_applies_when: No batch job, DAG, dbt model, Spark job or warehouse transformation is added, changed or described.
statements.text: dbt models over large fact tables MAY use `materialized='incremental'` with a `unique_key`, when a full refresh remains possible for backfills.
statements.title: Incremental models

statements.applies_when: the content is a design that proposes a new batch job, ETL pipeline or warehouse model.
statements.not_applies_when: No batch job, DAG, dbt model, Spark job or warehouse transformation is added, changed or described.
statements.text: A design for a new pipeline MUST state the schedule, the unit of rerun, the backfill procedure and the downstream consumers affected by a late or wrong run.
statements.title: Reprocessing in designs

statements.applies_when: markup or JSX adds an element with `onClick`, `@click` or a `click` event listener, or a custom button or link component.
statements.not_applies_when: No web user interface is added, changed or described (backend code, native mobile screens, infrastructure).
statements.text: Clickable controls MUST use a native `<button>` or `<a href>` element; a `div` or `span` with a click handler MUST NOT be used as a button or link.
statements.title: Native elements for controls

statements.applies_when: markup or JSX adds or changes a form field element or a text input component.
statements.not_applies_when: No web user interface is added, changed or described (backend code, native mobile screens, infrastructure).
statements.text: Every `<input>`, `<select>` and `<textarea>` MUST have an accessible name from a `<label for>`, a wrapping `<label>` or `aria-labelledby`; placeholder text alone MUST NOT act as the label.
statements.title: Labelled form fields

statements.applies_when: markup or JSX adds an `` element or an image component that renders one.
statements.not_applies_when: No web user interface is added, changed or described (backend code, native mobile screens, infrastructure).
statements.text: Every `` element MUST have an `alt` attribute; purely decorative images MUST use `alt=""`.
statements.title: Alt attribute on images

statements.applies_when: the content sets a non-empty `alt` value or an `aria-label` on an image or icon.
statements.not_applies_when: No web user interface is added, changed or described (backend code, native mobile screens, infrastructure).
statements.text: Alternative text for an informative image SHOULD describe its content or function (for example "Terrace of Le Petit Bistro") and SHOULD NOT repeat the file name or start with "image of".
statements.title: Meaningful alternative text

statements.applies_when: the content adds a custom interactive widget (dropdown, date picker, carousel, slot selector), a `keydown` handler or a `tabindex` attribute.
statements.not_applies_when: No web user interface is added, changed or described (backend code, native mobile screens, infrastructure).
statements.text: Every interactive element MUST be reachable and operable with the keyboard alone (Tab, Enter, Space, Escape, arrow keys for composite widgets), and `tabindex` values greater than 0 MUST NOT be used.
statements.title: Keyboard operable widgets

statements.applies_when: CSS, SCSS or a styled component sets `outline`, `box-shadow` or `border` on `:focus` or `:focus-visible`, or removes the outline of an element.
statements.not_applies_when: No web user interface is added, changed or described (backend code, native mobile screens, infrastructure).
statements.text: Focus MUST stay visible: a rule that removes the outline on `:focus` or `:focus-visible` (`outline: none`, `outline: 0`) MUST replace it with another visible focus style.
statements.title: Visible focus indicator

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes a modal, dialog, drawer, bottom sheet or overlay component on the web.
statements.not_applies_when: No web user interface is added, changed or described (backend code, native mobile screens, infrastructure).
statements.text: A modal dialog MUST move focus into itself when it opens, keep Tab inside it while open, close on Escape, and return focus to the element that opened it when it closes.
statements.title: Focus management in dialogs

statements.applies_when: the content sets a text colour, a background colour behind text, or opacity on text.
statements.not_applies_when: No web user interface is added, changed or described (backend code, native mobile screens, infrastructure).
statements.text: Text MUST meet WCAG 2.2 AA contrast against its background: 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for text of at least 24px or bold text of at least 18.66px.
statements.title: Text colour contrast

statements.applies_when: the content shows status, validation errors, availability or selection by changing a colour.
statements.not_applies_when: No web user interface is added, changed or described (backend code, native mobile screens, infrastructure).
statements.text: State such as an unavailable time slot, a form error or a selected filter SHOULD NOT be conveyed by colour alone; an icon, text or pattern SHOULD accompany the colour.
statements.title: Colour is not the only signal

statements.applies_when: markup or JSX adds a `role` attribute, an `aria-*` attribute or `aria-hidden`.
statements.not_applies_when: No web user interface is added, changed or described (backend code, native mobile screens, infrastructure).
statements.text: ARIA roles and attributes SHOULD be added only when no native HTML element provides the semantics, and an element with `aria-hidden="true"` SHOULD NOT contain focusable elements.
statements.title: ARIA only when native semantics are missing

statements.applies_when: the content shows a toast, inline status or error message after an asynchronous request completes.
statements.not_applies_when: No web user interface is added, changed or described (backend code, native mobile screens, infrastructure).
statements.text: Asynchronous status changes (booking confirmed, slot no longer available) MAY be announced through an `aria-live="polite"` region instead of moving focus to the message.
statements.title: Live announcements for async updates

statements.applies_when: the content adds an `Icon`, `IconButton`, `ImageButton`, `Image`, `UIButton` or SwiftUI `Button` that has no visible text.
statements.not_applies_when: No native mobile user interface is added, changed or described (web pages, backend code, build configuration).
statements.text: An icon-only button or tappable image MUST have an accessible label: `contentDescription` on Android, `accessibilityLabel` on iOS.
statements.title: Labels on icon-only controls

statements.applies_when: the content adds a background image, divider, illustration or other image that carries no information.
statements.not_applies_when: No native mobile user interface is added, changed or described (web pages, backend code, build configuration).
statements.text: Decorative images MUST be hidden from screen readers: `contentDescription = null` in Compose, `importantForAccessibility="no"` in Android XML, `.accessibilityHidden(true)` or `isAccessibilityElement = false` on iOS.
statements.title: Decorative images hidden

statements.applies_when: Android layout XML, a style resource or Compose code sets `textSize`, `fontSize` or a text style size.
statements.not_applies_when: No native mobile user interface is added, changed or described (web pages, backend code, build configuration).
statements.text: Android text sizes MUST be declared in `sp`; text sizes in `dp` or `px` MUST NOT be used.
statements.title: Scalable text units on Android

statements.applies_when: Swift code sets a font on a `Text`, `UILabel`, `UITextField` or `UIButton`, or creates a `UIFont` with a fixed size.
statements.not_applies_when: No native mobile user interface is added, changed or described (web pages, backend code, build configuration).
statements.text: iOS text MUST use Dynamic Type text styles (`.font(.body)`, `UIFont.preferredFont(forTextStyle:)` or `UIFontMetrics` for custom fonts), and UIKit labels MUST set `adjustsFontForContentSizeCategory = true`.
statements.title: Dynamic Type on iOS

statements.applies_when: the content sets a fixed height, `maxLines`, `lineLimit` or truncation on a view that contains text.
statements.not_applies_when: No native mobile user interface is added, changed or described (web pages, backend code, build configuration).
statements.text: Screens SHOULD remain usable at the largest accessibility text size (200% on Android, AX5 on iOS): text SHOULD wrap instead of being truncated, and text containers SHOULD NOT have fixed heights.
statements.title: Layout at the largest text size

statements.applies_when: the content adds or resizes a button, icon button, checkbox, chip, link or other tappable element in a mobile screen.
statements.not_applies_when: No native mobile user interface is added, changed or described (web pages, backend code, build configuration).
statements.text: Every interactive element MUST have a touch target of at least 48x48dp on Android and 44x44pt on iOS, extended with padding, `minimumInteractiveComponentSize()` or a larger hit area when the visible icon is smaller.
statements.title: Minimum touch target size

statements.applies_when: the content adds a card, list row or cell composed of several text and image elements.
statements.not_applies_when: No native mobile user interface is added, changed or described (web pages, backend code, build configuration).
statements.text: Elements that form one item, such as a restaurant card with name, rating and price, SHOULD be merged into one accessibility node (`Modifier.semantics(mergeDescendants = true)`, `.accessibilityElement(children: .combine)`).
statements.title: Grouped content read as one item

statements.applies_when: the content adds a swipe-to-delete, long-press menu, drag gesture or other gesture handler in a mobile screen.
statements.not_applies_when: No native mobile user interface is added, changed or described (web pages, backend code, build configuration).
statements.text: An action available only through swipe, long press or drag MUST also be available as a visible control or as a custom accessibility action (`customActions`, `.accessibilityAction`).
statements.title: Alternatives to custom gestures

statements.applies_when: the content builds a custom toggle, checkbox, radio button, segmented control or tab instead of using the platform component.
statements.not_applies_when: No native mobile user interface is added, changed or described (web pages, backend code, build configuration).
statements.text: Custom toggles, checkboxes, radio buttons and tabs MUST expose their role and their checked or selected state (`Modifier.toggleable`, `semantics { role = Role.Switch }`, `.accessibilityAddTraits(.isSelected)`).
statements.title: Role and state of custom controls

statements.applies_when: the content shows a snackbar, toast, banner or inline status after an asynchronous result in a mobile screen.
statements.not_applies_when: No native mobile user interface is added, changed or described (web pages, backend code, build configuration).
statements.text: A state change not tied to focus, such as "Booking confirmed" or "Slot no longer available", SHOULD be announced with a live region on Android (`semantics { liveRegion = LiveRegionMode.Polite }`) or `UIAccessibility.post(notification: .announcement, argument:)` on iOS.
statements.title: Announcing state changes

statements.applies_when: the content adds a transition, parallax, auto-playing or looping animation in a mobile screen.
statements.not_applies_when: No native mobile user interface is added, changed or described (web pages, backend code, build configuration).
statements.text: Non-essential animations MAY be replaced by a cross-fade or skipped when the system reduce-motion setting is on (`UIAccessibility.isReduceMotionEnabled`, animator duration scale of 0 on Android).
statements.title: Reduced motion

statements.applies_when: UI code (JSX/TSX, Compose, SwiftUI, UIKit, server-side templates) adds a literal text node, button label, title, placeholder, tooltip or error message.
statements.not_applies_when: No user-facing text, translation catalog or display formatting is added or changed (internal logs, backend-only data processing, infrastructure).
statements.text: Text shown to users MUST come from the translation catalog through the i18n API (`t('booking.confirm.title')`, `stringResource(R.string.x)`, `String(localized:)`); string literals MUST NOT be rendered directly as labels, titles, placeholders or error messages.
statements.title: No hard-coded user-facing strings

statements.applies_when: the content concatenates strings, uses template literals or `+` around translated text, or passes pieces of a sentence to several translation keys.
statements.not_applies_when: No user-facing text, translation catalog or display formatting is added or changed (internal logs, backend-only data processing, infrastructure).
statements.text: A translated sentence MUST be one message with named placeholders (`"Table for {guests} at {restaurantName}"`); sentences MUST NOT be built by concatenating translated fragments or joining them with variables.
statements.title: Whole sentences with named placeholders

statements.applies_when: the content displays a number of guests, bookings, reviews, points, days or any other count next to a noun.
statements.not_applies_when: No user-facing text, translation catalog or display formatting is added or changed (internal logs, backend-only data processing, infrastructure).
statements.text: Messages that contain a count MUST use ICU plural syntax (`{count, plural, one {# guest} other {# guests}}`) or platform plurals (`<plurals>` resources, `.stringsdict`, `^[]` inflection); a ternary on `count === 1` MUST NOT choose between two strings.
statements.title: Plural forms

statements.applies_when: the content formats a date, time, weekday or month name for display to a user.
statements.not_applies_when: No user-facing text, translation catalog or display formatting is added or changed (internal logs, backend-only data processing, infrastructure).
statements.text: Dates and times shown to users MUST be formatted with the active locale (`Intl.DateTimeFormat`, `DateTimeFormatter.ofLocalizedDate`, `DateFormatter` with a locale and a template); fixed patterns such as `DD/MM/YYYY`, `toISOString()` or `toLocaleDateString()` without a locale MUST NOT be displayed.
statements.title: Locale-aware dates and times

statements.applies_when: the content displays or converts the date or time of a booking, a time slot or opening hours.
statements.not_applies_when: No user-facing text, translation catalog or display formatting is added or changed (internal logs, backend-only data processing, infrastructure).
statements.text: Booking dates and times SHOULD be displayed in the restaurant's time zone, with the time zone name shown when it differs from the time zone of the device.
statements.title: Restaurant time zone for booking times

statements.applies_when: the content displays a price, a deposit, a discount amount, a bill total or loyalty value in money.
statements.not_applies_when: No user-facing text, translation catalog or display formatting is added or changed (internal logs, backend-only data processing, infrastructure).
statements.text: Prices MUST be formatted with a currency-aware formatter (`Intl.NumberFormat(locale, { style: 'currency', currency })`, `NumberFormat.getCurrencyInstance`, `.formatted(.currency(code:))`) using the currency code from the data; a hard-coded symbol such as `'€' + amount` MUST NOT be used.
statements.title: Currency-aware price formatting

statements.applies_when: the content displays a decimal number, a rating, a distance, a percentage or a large integer to users.
statements.not_applies_when: No user-facing text, translation catalog or display formatting is added or changed (internal logs, backend-only data processing, infrastructure).
statements.text: Numbers shown to users, such as ratings, distances and percentages, SHOULD be formatted with the locale's decimal and grouping separators rather than `toFixed()` or string interpolation.
statements.title: Locale-aware numbers

statements.applies_when: CSS or layout code sets left or right margins, padding, positions, floats, text alignment or `Gravity.LEFT`/`RIGHT`.
statements.not_applies_when: No user-facing text, translation catalog or display formatting is added or changed (internal logs, backend-only data processing, infrastructure).
statements.text: Layout SHOULD use logical directions (`margin-inline-start`, `padding-inline-end`, `inset-inline-start`, `text-align: start`, `start`/`end` in Compose and SwiftUI) instead of left and right, so that Arabic and Hebrew layouts mirror correctly.
statements.title: Logical properties for right-to-left layouts

statements.applies_when: the content changes the HTML document shell, the root layout component, or the code that switches the active locale.
statements.not_applies_when: No user-facing text, translation catalog or display formatting is added or changed (internal logs, backend-only data processing, infrastructure).
statements.text: The root `<html>` element MUST set `lang` and `dir` from the active locale, and a page that switches locale MUST update both.
statements.title: Language and direction on the document

statements.applies_when: the content adds or renames a call to the translation function or a string resource reference.
statements.not_applies_when: No user-facing text, translation catalog or display formatting is added or changed (internal logs, backend-only data processing, infrastructure).
statements.text: Every translation key referenced in code MUST exist in the English source catalog in the same change.
statements.title: Keys exist in the source catalog

statements.applies_when: the content renders restaurant data, menu items, reviews or other user-generated or partner-provided text.
statements.not_applies_when: No user-facing text, translation catalog or display formatting is added or changed (internal logs, backend-only data processing, infrastructure).
statements.text: Restaurant names, dish names, brand names and text entered by users MAY be rendered directly without going through the translation catalog.
statements.title: Content that is not translated

statements.applies_when: a `useEffect` or `useLayoutEffect` calls `setInterval`, `setTimeout`, `addEventListener`, `subscribe`, `new WebSocket` or `new EventSource`.
statements.not_applies_when: No React component or hook is added or changed (backend TypeScript, build scripts, plain utility modules, styles).
statements.text: A `useEffect` that subscribes to a store, starts a timer or interval, adds an event listener or opens a socket MUST return a cleanup function that undoes it.
statements.title: Effect cleanup

statements.applies_when: a `useEffect` calls `fetch`, `axios` or an API client and then sets state with the result.
statements.not_applies_when: No React component or hook is added or changed (backend TypeScript, build scripts, plain utility modules, styles).
statements.text: A `useEffect` that starts a fetch MUST abort it (`AbortController`) or ignore its result when the component unmounts or the dependencies change, so a stale response never overwrites newer state.
statements.title: Cancel or ignore stale requests

statements.applies_when: JSX renders a list with `.map()` or sets a `key` prop.
statements.not_applies_when: No React component or hook is added or changed (backend TypeScript, build scripts, plain utility modules, styles).
statements.text: Elements rendered from `.map()` MUST have a `key` taken from a stable id in the data (for example `restaurant.id`); the array index MUST NOT be used as the key of a list that can be reordered, filtered or inserted into.
statements.title: Stable list keys

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes the dependency array of `useEffect`, `useMemo`, `useCallback` or `useLayoutEffect`, or an `eslint-disable` comment for `react-hooks`.
statements.not_applies_when: No React component or hook is added or changed (backend TypeScript, build scripts, plain utility modules, styles).
statements.text: Hook dependency arrays MUST list every prop, state value and function from component scope that the hook reads, and the `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` rule MUST NOT be disabled with an eslint comment.
statements.title: Complete dependency arrays

statements.applies_when: a `useEffect` only calls a state setter with a value computed from props or other state.
statements.not_applies_when: No React component or hook is added or changed (backend TypeScript, build scripts, plain utility modules, styles).
statements.text: Values that can be computed from props or other state SHOULD be computed during render (with `useMemo` when expensive) instead of being copied into `useState` and synced by an effect.
statements.title: Derived values are computed, not synced

statements.applies_when: the content calls a `useState` setter or a reducer, or changes an object or array held in state, props or context.
statements.not_applies_when: No React component or hook is added or changed (backend TypeScript, build scripts, plain utility modules, styles).
statements.text: State objects and arrays MUST NOT be mutated in place (`items.push(x)`, `booking.status = 'x'` followed by a setter call); every update MUST produce a new object or array.
statements.title: No mutation of state

statements.applies_when: the content calls a function whose name starts with `use` inside a component or custom hook.
statements.not_applies_when: No React component or hook is added or changed (backend TypeScript, build scripts, plain utility modules, styles).
statements.text: Hooks MUST be called only at the top level of a function component or a custom hook, never inside conditions, loops, early returns or nested callbacks.
statements.title: Hooks at the top level

statements.applies_when: a component or hook fetches data from a backend API.
statements.not_applies_when: No React component or hook is added or changed (backend TypeScript, build scripts, plain utility modules, styles).
statements.text: Data from our APIs SHOULD be read through the shared TanStack Query hooks in `src/api/queries` rather than through hand-written `useEffect` and `useState` pairs.
statements.title: Shared data-fetching layer

statements.applies_when: the content adds a route, a page component or changes the router configuration.
statements.not_applies_when: No React component or hook is added or changed (backend TypeScript, build scripts, plain utility modules, styles).
statements.text: Each route-level page SHOULD be wrapped in an error boundary that renders a fallback UI, so that a render error in one widget does not blank the whole page.
statements.title: Error boundary per route

statements.applies_when: the content adds a React component or grows an existing one.
statements.not_applies_when: No React component or hook is added or changed (backend TypeScript, build scripts, plain utility modules, styles).
statements.text: A component file SHOULD NOT exceed 300 lines; a larger component SHOULD be split into smaller components or custom hooks.
statements.title: Component size

statements.applies_when: the content adds, removes or discusses `useMemo`, `useCallback` or `React.memo`.
statements.not_applies_when: No React component or hook is added or changed (backend TypeScript, build scripts, plain utility modules, styles).
statements.text: `useMemo` and `useCallback` MAY be omitted for cheap computations and for callbacks that are not passed to memoised children or used as hook dependencies.
statements.title: Memoisation is not a default

statements.applies_when: the content adds imports to client code, adds a client dependency, or changes the bundler configuration.
statements.not_applies_when: No browser-side code, page markup or client dependency is added or changed (backend services, mobile apps, infrastructure).
statements.text: The gzipped initial JavaScript of each route MUST stay within the budget declared in `bundle-budgets.json` (170 KB by default); the CI size check fails the build when it is exceeded.
statements.title: Route bundle budget

statements.applies_when: the content imports a new npm package in browser code or adds a dependency to the web app's `package.json`.
statements.not_applies_when: No browser-side code, page markup or client dependency is added or changed (backend services, mobile apps, infrastructure).
statements.text: A new client dependency larger than 30 KB gzipped SHOULD NOT be part of the initial bundle; it SHOULD be loaded with a dynamic `import()` at the point of use.
statements.title: Heavy dependencies loaded on demand

statements.applies_when: the content adds an `import` or `require` of a third-party library in browser code.
statements.not_applies_when: No browser-side code, page markup or client dependency is added or changed (backend services, mobile apps, infrastructure).
statements.text: Libraries MUST be imported by named ESM import or by module path (`import { format } from 'date-fns'`, `import debounce from 'lodash/debounce'`); whole packages (`import _ from 'lodash'`, `import * as icons from '...'`) MUST NOT be imported.
statements.title: Tree-shakable imports

statements.applies_when: the content adds a route, a page component or a large widget such as a map, gallery or carousel.
statements.not_applies_when: No browser-side code, page markup or client dependency is added or changed (backend services, mobile apps, infrastructure).
statements.text: Route-level pages and below-the-fold widgets (map, photo gallery, reviews carousel) SHOULD be code-split with `React.lazy` or dynamic `import()`.
statements.title: Code-split routes and heavy widgets

statements.applies_when: markup or JSX adds an ``, `` or image component.
statements.not_applies_when: No browser-side code, page markup or client dependency is added or changed (backend services, mobile apps, infrastructure).
statements.text: Every `` MUST declare `width` and `height` attributes or sit in a box with a fixed `aspect-ratio`, so the layout does not shift when the image loads.
statements.title: Sized images

statements.applies_when: markup or JSX adds an `` or `
statements.not_applies_when: No browser-side code, page markup or client dependency is added or changed (backend services, mobile apps, infrastructure).
statements.text: Images and iframes below the fold SHOULD use `loading="lazy"`.
statements.title: Lazy loading below the fold

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes the hero, header or first image of a page.
statements.not_applies_when: No browser-side code, page markup or client dependency is added or changed (backend services, mobile apps, infrastructure).
statements.text: The largest above-the-fold image of a page (the LCP element, such as the restaurant hero photo) MUST NOT use `loading="lazy"` and MUST NOT be injected by client-side JavaScript after hydration.
statements.title: Hero image loads eagerly

statements.applies_when: the content renders a restaurant, dish, user or partner photo on a web page.
statements.not_applies_when: No browser-side code, page markup or client dependency is added or changed (backend services, mobile apps, infrastructure).
statements.text: Restaurant and dish photos MUST be served through the image CDN with `srcset` and `sizes` and in AVIF or WebP; the original upload URL MUST NOT be used in an ``.
statements.title: Images through the image CDN

statements.applies_when: an event handler, input handler or effect loops over large arrays, parses large payloads or does heavy computation in the browser.
statements.not_applies_when: No browser-side code, page markup or client dependency is added or changed (backend services, mobile apps, infrastructure).
statements.text: Event-handler work longer than about 50 ms (sorting thousands of slots, parsing large JSON, filtering big lists) SHOULD be chunked, deferred with `requestIdleCallback` or `scheduler.yield()`, or moved to a Web Worker.
statements.title: Short main-thread tasks

statements.applies_when: the content adds a `<script>` tag, a script loader call or a third-party snippet to a page.
statements.not_applies_when: No browser-side code, page markup or client dependency is added or changed (backend services, mobile apps, infrastructure).
statements.text: Third-party scripts (tag managers, chat widgets, ads, A/B testing) MUST be loaded with `async` or `defer`, or after user interaction; they MUST NOT be render-blocking `<script>` tags in `<head>`.
statements.title: Non-blocking third-party scripts

statements.applies_when: the content changes the document `<head>` or adds `<link rel>` hints.
statements.not_applies_when: No browser-side code, page markup or client dependency is added or changed (backend services, mobile apps, infrastructure).
statements.text: A page MAY add `<link rel="preconnect">` or `<link rel="preload">` for the image CDN and the API origin that it uses above the fold.
statements.title: Resource hints

statements.applies_when: CSS, SCSS or CSS-in-JS sets `color`, `background`, `border-color`, `fill`, `stroke` or `box-shadow` colour values.
statements.not_applies_when: No styles or style values are added or changed (component logic without styling, backend code, mobile apps).
statements.text: Colours in component styles MUST come from design tokens (`var(--color-text-primary)`, `theme.colors.primary`); raw hex, `rgb()`, `hsl()` or named colours MUST NOT be used.
statements.title: Colours from tokens

statements.applies_when: CSS, SCSS or CSS-in-JS sets `margin`, `padding`, `gap`, `top`/`left` offsets or grid gaps.
statements.not_applies_when: No styles or style values are added or changed (component logic without styling, backend code, mobile apps).
statements.text: Margins, paddings and gaps SHOULD use spacing tokens (`var(--space-4)`, `theme.space[2]`) instead of raw pixel or rem values.
statements.title: Spacing from the spacing scale

statements.applies_when: CSS, SCSS or CSS-in-JS sets `font-family`, `font-size`, `font-weight`, `line-height` or the `font` shorthand.
statements.not_applies_when: No styles or style values are added or changed (component logic without styling, backend code, mobile apps).
statements.text: Font family, size, weight and line height MUST come from typography tokens or the `text-style()` mixin; components MUST NOT declare their own `font-family`.
statements.title: Typography from tokens

statements.applies_when: CSS, SCSS or CSS-in-JS contains `!important`.
statements.not_applies_when: No styles or style values are added or changed (component logic without styling, backend code, mobile apps).
statements.text: Component styles MUST NOT use `!important`.
statements.title: No !important

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes an `@media` query, a container query or a breakpoint helper call.
statements.not_applies_when: No styles or style values are added or changed (component logic without styling, backend code, mobile apps).
statements.text: Media queries MUST use the shared breakpoint mixins or tokens (`@include bp(md)`, `theme.breakpoints.up('md')`); ad-hoc pixel widths such as `@media (max-width: 767px)` MUST NOT be used.
statements.title: Shared breakpoints

statements.applies_when: the content adds responsive styles or `max-width` media queries.
statements.not_applies_when: No styles or style values are added or changed (component logic without styling, backend code, mobile apps).
statements.text: Responsive styles SHOULD be written mobile-first: base styles for small screens and `min-width` breakpoints for larger ones.
statements.title: Mobile-first media queries

statements.applies_when: component styles reference a colour token or palette variable.
statements.not_applies_when: No styles or style values are added or changed (component logic without styling, backend code, mobile apps).
statements.text: Components MUST use semantic tokens (`--color-surface`, `--color-text-muted`) that have a dark theme value; primitive palette tokens (`--palette-grey-900`) MUST NOT be used directly in components.
statements.title: Semantic tokens for dark mode

statements.applies_when: the content adds a `prefers-color-scheme` media query, a `matchMedia` call for colour scheme, or theme-dependent styles in a component.
statements.not_applies_when: No styles or style values are added or changed (component logic without styling, backend code, mobile apps).
statements.text: Components SHOULD NOT read `prefers-color-scheme` directly; dark mode is applied by the `data-theme` attribute that the app shell sets on the root element.
statements.title: Theme switching through the app shell

statements.applies_when: CSS, SCSS or CSS-in-JS sets a `font-size`.
statements.not_applies_when: No styles or style values are added or changed (component logic without styling, backend code, mobile apps).
statements.text: Font sizes SHOULD be expressed in `rem` (usually through tokens) so that the user's browser font setting applies; `px` font sizes SHOULD NOT be used.
statements.title: Relative font sizes

statements.applies_when: CSS, SCSS or CSS-in-JS sets `z-index`.
statements.not_applies_when: No styles or style values are added or changed (component logic without styling, backend code, mobile apps).
statements.text: `z-index` values MUST come from the layer tokens (`--z-dropdown`, `--z-modal`, `--z-toast`); arbitrary values such as `z-index: 9999` MUST NOT be used.
statements.title: z-index from the layer scale

statements.applies_when: the content declares a new CSS custom property (`--name: value`) inside a component stylesheet.
statements.not_applies_when: No styles or style values are added or changed (component logic without styling, backend code, mobile apps).
statements.text: A component MAY define its own CSS custom property for a value local to that component (for example `--card-image-height`) when no design token exists for it, as long as the value is not a colour.
statements.title: Local custom properties

statements.applies_when: the content adds a component that renders a button, text input, select, modal, date picker, toast, tabs, chip or similar UI primitive.
statements.not_applies_when: No user interface component, icon or design system dependency is added, changed or described.
statements.text: UI MUST use the design system component (`Button`, `TextField`, `Modal`, `DatePicker`, `Toast`, `Tabs`) when one exists for the need; a custom re-implementation of the same control MUST NOT be added.
statements.title: Design system component first

statements.applies_when: the content passes `className`, `style`, `sx` or a styled wrapper to a design system component.
statements.not_applies_when: No user interface component, icon or design system dependency is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Design system components SHOULD be customised through their `variant`, `size` and `tone` props, not by overriding their internal styles with `className`, `style` or nested selectors.
statements.title: Variants instead of overrides

statements.applies_when: the content adds an import from a design system package.
statements.not_applies_when: No user interface component, icon or design system dependency is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Design system components MUST be imported from the package entry point (`@acme/design-system`); internal paths such as `@acme/design-system/dist/...` or `/src/...` MUST NOT be imported.
statements.title: Public entry points only

statements.applies_when: the content changes the design system dependency in `package.json`, `build.gradle(.kts)` or `Package.swift`.
statements.not_applies_when: No user interface component, icon or design system dependency is added, changed or described.
statements.text: An application MUST depend on a single major version of the design system; two major versions MUST NOT be bundled together.
statements.title: One major version per app
