statements.applies_when: the content adds a web component whose markup is mostly `div` and `span` elements with custom class names.
statements.not_applies_when: No user interface component, icon or design system dependency is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Product components SHOULD be composed from the design system layout primitives (`Stack`, `Box`, `Text`) rather than raw `div` or `span` elements with custom CSS.
statements.title: Layout primitives over raw containers

statements.applies_when: the content adds an icon, an inline `<svg>`, an icon font or an icon library dependency.
statements.not_applies_when: No user interface component, icon or design system dependency is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Icons MUST come from the design system icon set; inline SVG icons, icon fonts or third-party icon packages MUST NOT be added to product code.
statements.title: Icons from the icon set

statements.applies_when: Kotlin or Swift code adds a `Button`, `TextField`, `AlertDialog`, `ModalBottomSheet`, `UIButton` or `UIAlertController`.
statements.not_applies_when: No user interface component, icon or design system dependency is added, changed or described.
statements.text: The Android and iOS apps MUST use the Compose and SwiftUI design system libraries for buttons, text fields, dialogs and bottom sheets instead of raw Material or UIKit components.
statements.title: Native design system libraries

statements.applies_when: the content adds a new generic UI component in a product repository.
statements.not_applies_when: No user interface component, icon or design system dependency is added, changed or described.
statements.text: When no design system component fits, the team SHOULD open a request in the design system repository and place the local component under `src/ui/local/` with a comment linking to that request.
statements.title: Requesting a missing component

statements.applies_when: the content is a design spec that describes new screens, flows or UI patterns.
statements.not_applies_when: No user interface component, icon or design system dependency is added, changed or described.
statements.text: A design spec that introduces a new UI pattern SHOULD list the design system components it uses and any new component it needs from the design system team.
statements.title: Components listed in UI specs

statements.applies_when: the content adds UI for an A/B test or experiment behind a feature flag.
statements.not_applies_when: No user interface component, icon or design system dependency is added, changed or described.
statements.text: An experiment behind a feature flag MAY use local components for up to one quarter before it is moved to design system components or removed.
statements.title: Experiments behind a flag

statements.applies_when: Kotlin code references `GlobalScope`.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not Kotlin code of an Android app (Kotlin backend services, iOS, web).
statements.text: `GlobalScope.launch` and `GlobalScope.async` MUST NOT be used in app code.
statements.title: No GlobalScope

statements.applies_when: Kotlin code calls `launch`, `async` or creates a `CoroutineScope`.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not Kotlin code of an Android app (Kotlin backend services, iOS, web).
statements.text: Coroutines MUST be launched in `viewModelScope`, `lifecycleScope` or an injected `CoroutineScope` tied to a component lifecycle; a new unowned `CoroutineScope(...)` MUST NOT be created inside a function.
statements.title: Structured coroutine scopes

statements.applies_when: an Activity, Fragment or composable calls `collect`, `collectLatest`, `collectAsState` or `observe` on a flow or LiveData.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not Kotlin code of an Android app (Kotlin backend services, iOS, web).
statements.text: A flow collected in an Activity or Fragment MUST be collected inside `repeatOnLifecycle(Lifecycle.State.STARTED)`, and a flow read in Compose MUST use `collectAsStateWithLifecycle()`.
statements.title: Lifecycle-aware flow collection

statements.applies_when: Kotlin code reads or writes files, SharedPreferences, DataStore or Room, performs a network call, or calls `runBlocking`.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not Kotlin code of an Android app (Kotlin backend services, iOS, web).
statements.text: Disk, database and network work MUST NOT run on the main thread; it MUST run in a `suspend` function that switches to an IO dispatcher with `withContext`.
statements.title: No blocking work on the main thread

statements.applies_when: a ViewModel, repository or use case references `Dispatchers.IO`, `Dispatchers.Default` or `Dispatchers.Main`.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not Kotlin code of an Android app (Kotlin backend services, iOS, web).
statements.text: Dispatchers SHOULD be injected through the constructor instead of referencing `Dispatchers.IO` or `Dispatchers.Default` directly, so tests can pass a test dispatcher.
statements.title: Injected dispatchers

statements.applies_when: the content adds state to an Activity, Fragment or screen composable, or adds a ViewModel.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not Kotlin code of an Android app (Kotlin backend services, iOS, web).
statements.text: Screen state MUST live in a `ViewModel` and be exposed as a `StateFlow`, not in Activity, Fragment or composable fields, so that it survives configuration changes.
statements.title: Screen state in a ViewModel

statements.applies_when: a ViewModel declares a public or internal `MutableStateFlow`, `MutableSharedFlow` or `MutableLiveData`.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not Kotlin code of an Android app (Kotlin backend services, iOS, web).
statements.text: `MutableStateFlow`, `MutableSharedFlow` and `MutableLiveData` SHOULD be private and exposed through a read-only `StateFlow`, `SharedFlow` or `LiveData` property.
statements.title: Read-only state exposure

statements.applies_when: a ViewModel constructor or property has a type of `Context`, `Activity`, `Fragment`, `View` or a UI callback.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not Kotlin code of an Android app (Kotlin backend services, iOS, web).
statements.text: A ViewModel MUST NOT hold a reference to an Activity, Fragment, View, composable lambda or Activity `Context`.
statements.title: No UI references in ViewModels

statements.applies_when: the content requests a runtime permission, checks `checkSelfPermission`, or adds a permission to `AndroidManifest.xml`.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not Kotlin code of an Android app (Kotlin backend services, iOS, web).
statements.text: Dangerous permissions (location, camera, contacts, `POST_NOTIFICATIONS` on Android 13+) MUST be requested when the feature is used, through `registerForActivityResult` with `RequestPermission`, and the denied case MUST be handled without crashing.
statements.title: Runtime permissions at the point of use

statements.applies_when: a `suspend` function or coroutine body contains `catch (e: Exception)`, `catch (e: Throwable)` or `runCatching`.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not Kotlin code of an Android app (Kotlin backend services, iOS, web).
statements.text: Code that catches `Exception` or `Throwable` inside a coroutine MUST rethrow `CancellationException`.
statements.title: Rethrow cancellation

statements.applies_when: the content handles a denied runtime permission or requests a permission a second time.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not Kotlin code of an Android app (Kotlin backend services, iOS, web).
statements.text: Before asking again for a permission the user denied, the app SHOULD show a rationale when `shouldShowRequestPermissionRationale` returns true.
statements.title: Permission rationale

statements.applies_when: Swift code adds or changes an `ObservableObject`, `@Observable` class, view controller, or code that updates UI after a network or background call.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not Swift code of an iOS app (Android, web, backend services).
statements.text: Types that own UI state (observable view models, `UIViewController` subclasses) MUST be annotated `@MainActor`, and UIKit or SwiftUI state MUST NOT be changed from a background thread.
statements.title: UI state on the main actor

statements.applies_when: async Swift code calls `DispatchQueue.main.async` or `DispatchQueue.main.sync`.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not Swift code of an iOS app (Android, web, backend services).
statements.text: In async code, returning to the main thread SHOULD use `@MainActor` functions or `await MainActor.run` instead of `DispatchQueue.main.async`.
statements.title: Main-actor hops in async code

statements.applies_when: Swift code passes a closure that references `self` to `sink`, `addObserver`, `Timer.scheduledTimer` or stores it in a property.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not Swift code of an iOS app (Android, web, backend services).
statements.text: An escaping closure that is stored by an object (completion handler property, Combine `sink`, `NotificationCenter` observer, `Timer`) and captures `self` MUST capture it as `[weak self]`.
statements.title: Weak self in stored escaping closures

statements.applies_when: Swift code declares a `delegate` or `dataSource` property or a delegate protocol.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not Swift code of an iOS app (Android, web, backend services).
statements.text: Delegate and data source properties MUST be declared `weak var` with a class-bound protocol (`protocol BookingDelegate: AnyObject`).
statements.title: Weak delegates

statements.applies_when: Swift code stores or reads an authentication token, refresh token, session id or API credential.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not Swift code of an iOS app (Android, web, backend services).
statements.text: Access tokens, refresh tokens and session identifiers MUST be stored in the Keychain with `kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly` or a stricter class, and MUST NOT be stored in `UserDefaults`, `@AppStorage`, plist files or the file system.
statements.title: Tokens in the Keychain

statements.applies_when: Swift code creates a `Task { }` or `Task.detached` in a view, view controller or view model.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not Swift code of an iOS app (Android, web, backend services).
statements.text: A `Task` started from a view or view model SHOULD be stored and cancelled when the view disappears, or started with the SwiftUI `.task` modifier, which cancels it automatically.
statements.title: Cancelled tasks

statements.applies_when: Swift code adds a function with a completion handler, `@escaping` result callback or a new async function.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not Swift code of an iOS app (Android, web, backend services).
statements.text: New asynchronous APIs SHOULD be written as `async` functions instead of functions that take a completion handler.
statements.title: Async functions for new APIs

statements.applies_when: Swift code calls `withCheckedContinuation`, `withCheckedThrowingContinuation` or `withUnsafeContinuation`.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not Swift code of an iOS app (Android, web, backend services).
statements.text: A `withCheckedContinuation` or `withCheckedThrowingContinuation` block MUST resume its continuation exactly once on every code path, including error and early-return paths.
statements.title: Continuations resumed exactly once

statements.applies_when: Swift code contains a force unwrap, `try!` or `as!`.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not Swift code of an iOS app (Android, web, backend services).
statements.text: Force unwraps (`!`), `try!` and `as!` MUST NOT be used in app code outside tests and `@IBOutlet` declarations.
statements.title: No force unwraps

statements.applies_when: Swift code bridges a completion-handler or delegate-based API to async/await.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not Swift code of an iOS app (Android, web, backend services).
statements.text: An existing completion-handler API MAY be exposed to async code by wrapping it with `withCheckedThrowingContinuation` instead of rewriting it.
statements.title: Wrapping callback APIs

statements.applies_when: Swift code passes a value into a `Task`, an actor method or across an actor boundary, or changes Swift concurrency build settings.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not Swift code of an iOS app (Android, web, backend services).
statements.text: Types passed between actors or into detached tasks SHOULD conform to `Sendable`, and new modules SHOULD compile with strict concurrency checking set to `complete`.
statements.title: Sendable values across actors

statements.applies_when: the content adds a new notification type, campaign or template, or changes the category of one.
statements.not_applies_when: No email, push notification or SMS is sent, scheduled, templated, configured or described (in-app UI text, internal alerts to engineers).
statements.text: Every notification type MUST be declared in the notification catalog as `transactional` (booking confirmation, reminder, cancellation, receipt) or `marketing` (promotions, newsletters, recommendations).
statements.title: Declared message category

statements.applies_when: the content sends a marketing message, builds a campaign audience or schedules a batch of marketing sends.
statements.not_applies_when: No email, push notification or SMS is sent, scheduled, templated, configured or described (in-app UI text, internal alerts to engineers).
statements.text: Marketing emails, pushes and SMS MUST be sent only to users with an active opt-in for that channel, checked at send time and not only when the audience is built.
statements.title: Marketing opt-in checked at send time

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes a marketing email template, email headers or the unsubscribe handler.
statements.not_applies_when: No email, push notification or SMS is sent, scheduled, templated, configured or described (in-app UI text, internal alerts to engineers).
statements.text: Every marketing email MUST contain a one-click unsubscribe link and the `List-Unsubscribe` and `List-Unsubscribe-Post` headers, and an unsubscribe MUST take effect within 24 hours.
statements.title: One-click unsubscribe

statements.applies_when: the content adds content blocks, offers or recommendations to a booking confirmation, reminder, cancellation or receipt template.
statements.not_applies_when: No email, push notification or SMS is sent, scheduled, templated, configured or described (in-app UI text, internal alerts to engineers).
statements.text: Transactional messages SHOULD NOT contain promotional blocks such as offers or restaurant suggestions; a message with promotions is treated as marketing.
statements.title: No promotions in transactional messages

statements.applies_when: the content sends or schedules a push notification or SMS, or changes send-time scheduling.
statements.not_applies_when: No email, push notification or SMS is sent, scheduled, templated, configured or described (in-app UI text, internal alerts to engineers).
statements.text: Push notifications and SMS that are not time-critical MUST NOT be delivered between 21:00 and 08:00 in the recipient's local time zone; they are deferred to 08:00.
statements.title: Quiet hours

statements.applies_when: the content triggers a notification from an event consumer, a scheduled job, a retry or a webhook.
statements.not_applies_when: No email, push notification or SMS is sent, scheduled, templated, configured or described (in-app UI text, internal alerts to engineers).
statements.text: Each send MUST carry a deduplication key built from the notification type and the business event (for example `booking-reminder:{bookingId}`), and the sender MUST drop a second send with the same key within 24 hours.
statements.title: Deduplication key

statements.applies_when: the content schedules marketing push campaigns or changes frequency capping rules.
statements.not_applies_when: No email, push notification or SMS is sent, scheduled, templated, configured or described (in-app UI text, internal alerts to engineers).
statements.text: Marketing push notifications SHOULD be capped at two per user per week across all campaigns.
statements.title: Marketing frequency cap

statements.applies_when: the content builds the subject, title or body of an email, push notification or SMS.
statements.not_applies_when: No email, push notification or SMS is sent, scheduled, templated, configured or described (in-app UI text, internal alerts to engineers).
statements.text: Message content MUST be rendered from versioned, localised templates in the template service; message bodies MUST NOT be built as inline strings in service code.
statements.title: Versioned templates

statements.applies_when: an email template inserts a variable, or the content disables auto-escaping in a template.
statements.not_applies_when: No email, push notification or SMS is sent, scheduled, templated, configured or described (in-app UI text, internal alerts to engineers).
statements.text: Template variables that hold user or partner content (diner name, restaurant name, review text, special requests) MUST be HTML-escaped in email templates.
statements.title: Escaped template variables

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes the text of an SMS template.
statements.not_applies_when: No email, push notification or SMS is sent, scheduled, templated, configured or described (in-app UI text, internal alerts to engineers).
statements.text: SMS text SHOULD fit in one 160-character GSM-7 segment in every supported language.
statements.title: Single-segment SMS

statements.applies_when: the content sends an urgent booking change, cancellation or no-show message by push notification or SMS.
statements.not_applies_when: No email, push notification or SMS is sent, scheduled, templated, configured or described (in-app UI text, internal alerts to engineers).
statements.text: Critical transactional messages, such as a booking cancelled by the restaurant less than two hours before the booking time, MAY be delivered during quiet hours.
statements.title: Critical messages during quiet hours

statements.applies_when: the content adds, initialises or configures an analytics, advertising, attribution or session-replay SDK or tag, or sends tracking events.
statements.not_applies_when: No personal data is collected, stored, shared, exported, retained or deleted and no user tracking is added or changed.
statements.text: Analytics, advertising and session-replay SDKs (Google Analytics, Meta Pixel, Amplitude, Hotjar) MUST NOT be initialised or send events before the user has granted consent for that purpose in the consent management platform.
statements.title: Consent before tracking

statements.applies_when: the content reads the consent state or gates a feature on user consent.
statements.not_applies_when: No personal data is collected, stored, shared, exported, retained or deleted and no user tracking is added or changed.
statements.text: Code MUST check the consent for the specific purpose (`analytics`, `advertising`, `personalisation`) rather than one global consent flag.
statements.title: Purpose-specific consent checks

statements.applies_when: the content adds a form field, API field, database column or event property that holds personal data.
statements.not_applies_when: No personal data is collected, stored, shared, exported, retained or deleted and no user tracking is added or changed.
statements.text: A new field of personal data (phone number, birth date, dining preferences, precise location) MUST have a documented purpose in the data inventory, and a field not needed for that purpose MUST NOT be collected.
statements.title: Documented purpose for new personal data

statements.applies_when: the content collects or stores allergies, dietary needs, accessibility needs or other health-related information.
statements.not_applies_when: No personal data is collected, stored, shared, exported, retained or deleted and no user tracking is added or changed.
statements.text: Health data, such as allergies or medical dietary needs, MUST NOT be stored on the user profile without the user's explicit consent for that purpose.
statements.title: Special category data

statements.applies_when: the content creates a table, bucket, search index, cache or topic that stores personal data, or changes its retention.
statements.not_applies_when: No personal data is collected, stored, shared, exported, retained or deleted and no user tracking is added or changed.
statements.text: Every table, bucket, index or topic that holds personal data MUST have a defined retention period, and a TTL or scheduled job MUST delete or anonymise records older than that period.
statements.title: Retention period for every store

statements.applies_when: the content adds a new database, table, bucket or third-party system that stores data linked to a user id, email or phone number.
statements.not_applies_when: No personal data is collected, stored, shared, exported, retained or deleted and no user tracking is added or changed.
statements.text: A new store of personal data MUST be registered with the data subject request service so that access and export requests include its data.
statements.title: Stores registered for access requests

statements.applies_when: the content handles account deletion, erasure requests, or adds a copy of user data to another store.
statements.not_applies_when: No personal data is collected, stored, shared, exported, retained or deleted and no user tracking is added or changed.
statements.text: An account deletion request MUST remove or anonymise the user's data in every store within 30 days, including search indexes, caches, warehouse tables and processors.
statements.title: Deletion reaches every copy

statements.applies_when: the content sends user data to a third-party service, adds a third-party SDK that receives user data, or describes a new vendor integration.
statements.not_applies_when: No personal data is collected, stored, shared, exported, retained or deleted and no user tracking is added or changed.
statements.text: Personal data MUST NOT be sent to a new third-party processor (SaaS tool, SDK or external API) before a data processing agreement is signed and the processor is listed in the processor register.
statements.title: Processors under contract

statements.applies_when: the content exports user-level data to the warehouse, an analytics tool or a data science dataset.
statements.not_applies_when: No personal data is collected, stored, shared, exported, retained or deleted and no user tracking is added or changed.
statements.text: Data exported to the data warehouse or to analytics tools SHOULD identify users by a pseudonymous id instead of email address or phone number.
statements.title: Pseudonymous ids in analytics

statements.applies_when: the content copies, dumps, restores or seeds data from production into another environment.
statements.not_applies_when: No personal data is collected, stored, shared, exported, retained or deleted and no user tracking is added or changed.
statements.text: Production personal data SHOULD NOT be copied to staging, development or local environments; synthetic or anonymised datasets are used instead.
statements.title: No production personal data outside production

statements.applies_when: the content computes or stores aggregated statistics from personal data, or applies retention to aggregate tables.
statements.not_applies_when: No personal data is collected, stored, shared, exported, retained or deleted and no user tracking is added or changed.
statements.text: Aggregated statistics with no user-level rows, such as bookings per city per day, MAY be kept beyond the retention period of the personal data they were computed from.
statements.title: Aggregates beyond retention

statements.applies_when: the diff adds or changes an `if`/`switch`/`when` branch, a thrown or returned error, or a calculation in non-test source code.
statements.not_applies_when: the diff only renames, moves or reformats code without changing behavior.
statements.text: A change that adds or changes a branch, error path or business rule in production code MUST add or update a unit or integration test that fails without the change.
statements.title: Tests for new behavior

statements.applies_when: the change is described as a fix, references a bug ticket, or changes code to correct wrong behavior.
statements.not_applies_when: The content only changes documentation, comments, or configuration with no testable behavior, and touches no test files.
statements.text: A bug fix MUST include a test that reproduces the reported failure and passes only with the fix.
statements.title: Regression test for bug fixes

statements.applies_when: a test file calls `sleep`, `Thread.sleep`, `time.sleep`, `delay`, `setTimeout` or `asyncio.sleep` with a constant duration.
statements.not_applies_when: The content only changes documentation, comments, or configuration with no testable behavior, and touches no test files.
statements.text: Tests MUST NOT wait with a fixed sleep (`sleep`, `Thread.sleep`, `time.sleep`, `setTimeout` in a test body, `delay`); they wait for a condition with a polling helper and a timeout, or use a fake clock.
statements.title: No fixed sleeps in tests

statements.applies_when: a test or the code it covers calls `now()`, `Date.now`, `new Date()`, `Instant.now`, `time.Now`, `datetime.now` or `System.currentTimeMillis`.
statements.not_applies_when: The content only changes documentation, comments, or configuration with no testable behavior, and touches no test files.
statements.text: Code under test that reads the current time MUST receive it from an injected clock, and tests MUST set that clock to a fixed instant instead of reading the real system time.
statements.title: Deterministic time

statements.applies_when: a test or fixture uses `random`, `Math.random`, `Random()`, `rand`, `uuid4`, Faker or property-based test generators.
statements.not_applies_when: The content only changes documentation, comments, or configuration with no testable behavior, and touches no test files.
statements.text: Tests that use random values MUST use a fixed seed or a seeded generator, and the seed MUST be printed on failure so the case can be replayed.
statements.title: Seeded randomness

statements.applies_when: a test fixture, snapshot, seed file or test body contains names, email addresses, phone numbers, postal addresses or payment card numbers.
statements.not_applies_when: The content only changes documentation, comments, or configuration with no testable behavior, and touches no test files.
statements.text: Fixtures, snapshots and seed files MUST NOT contain real personal data copied from production; names, emails, phone numbers and addresses in tests are synthetic, and email domains use `example.com` or another reserved domain.
statements.title: Synthetic test data only

statements.applies_when: a test reads shared database rows, static or global variables, or files written by another test, or a test suite sets a fixed execution order.
statements.not_applies_when: The content only changes documentation, comments, or configuration with no testable behavior, and touches no test files.
statements.text: Each test SHOULD create the state it needs and SHOULD NOT depend on data left by another test or on the order in which tests run.
statements.title: Test isolation

statements.applies_when: an integration test configures a database, Kafka or Redis connection, or uses H2, SQLite, an in-memory broker or an embedded fake in place of the production engine.
statements.not_applies_when: The content only changes documentation, comments, or configuration with no testable behavior, and touches no test files.
statements.text: Integration tests of database or broker access SHOULD run against a real engine of the same major version started in a container (Testcontainers or docker compose), not an in-memory substitute such as H2 or SQLite.
statements.title: Real dependencies in integration tests

statements.applies_when: a test body contains only mock verifications (`verify`, `toHaveBeenCalled`, `assert_called`) and no assertion on a result.
statements.not_applies_when: The content only changes documentation, comments, or configuration with no testable behavior, and touches no test files.
statements.text: A test SHOULD assert on returned values, stored state or emitted messages, and SHOULD NOT only verify that internal collaborators were called.
statements.title: Assertions on behavior

statements.applies_when: a diff skips, disables or tags a test as flaky, quarantined or ignored (`@Disabled`, `skip`, `xit`, `t.Skip`, `pytest.mark.skip`).
statements.not_applies_when: The content only changes documentation, comments, or configuration with no testable behavior, and touches no test files.
statements.text: A test that is known to be flaky MAY be moved to a quarantine suite that does not block merges, when the move links a ticket with an owner who will fix or delete it.
statements.title: Quarantine of flaky tests

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes a user flow for search, booking, payment, cancellation or restaurant sign-in, or removes an end-to-end test of one.
statements.not_applies_when: No end-to-end test, contract test or cross-service interface is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Each critical user journey (search, booking, payment, cancellation, restaurant sign-in) MUST have at least one end-to-end test that runs against staging before every production deploy of the services it touches.
statements.title: Critical journeys covered

statements.applies_when: an end-to-end test uses a locator such as `page.locator`, `cy.get`, `onView`, `XCUIElement` query or `find_element`.
statements.not_applies_when: No end-to-end test, contract test or cross-service interface is added, changed or described.
statements.text: End-to-end tests MUST locate elements by test id or accessible role and name, and MUST NOT use CSS class names, XPath positions or visible copy that is translated.
statements.title: Stable selectors

statements.applies_when: an end-to-end test calls `waitForTimeout`, `cy.wait` with a number, `Thread.sleep` or `sleep`.
statements.not_applies_when: No end-to-end test, contract test or cross-service interface is added, changed or described.
statements.text: End-to-end tests MUST wait for a visible state (element shown, network response, navigation) and MUST NOT use fixed pauses such as `waitForTimeout` or `cy.wait(<number>)`.
statements.title: Explicit waits in UI tests

statements.applies_when: an end-to-end test signs in, books a table, or uses a hard-coded test user, restaurant id or account email.
statements.not_applies_when: No end-to-end test, contract test or cross-service interface is added, changed or described.
statements.text: End-to-end tests MUST create or lease their own diner and restaurant test accounts per run, and MUST NOT share a single account across parallel runs.
statements.title: Isolated test accounts

statements.applies_when: an end-to-end test goes through payment, prepayment, deposit or notification sending steps.
statements.not_applies_when: No end-to-end test, contract test or cross-service interface is added, changed or described.
statements.text: End-to-end tests MUST use the payment provider's sandbox and a sink for emails, SMS and push notifications, so that no real charge or message reaches a real person.
statements.title: No real payment or messages

statements.applies_when: the content adds a client for an internal HTTP API, or a consumer of an internal Kafka topic, owned by another team.
statements.not_applies_when: No end-to-end test, contract test or cross-service interface is added, changed or described.
statements.text: A service that starts consuming another internal service's HTTP API or Kafka event MUST publish a consumer contract (Pact or a schema compatibility test) that the provider's CI verifies.
statements.title: Consumer contract for new integrations

statements.applies_when: the content changes a CI workflow of a service that exposes an HTTP API or produces Kafka events consumed by other services, or disables contract verification.
statements.not_applies_when: No end-to-end test, contract test or cross-service interface is added, changed or described.
statements.text: A provider MUST run verification of all published consumer contracts in its pull request pipeline, and a failing verification MUST block the merge.
statements.title: Provider verification before merge

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes a Pact interaction, contract file or schema test with expected response bodies.
statements.not_applies_when: No end-to-end test, contract test or cross-service interface is added, changed or described.
statements.text: A consumer contract SHOULD cover only the fields and status codes that the consumer actually reads, so that providers can add fields freely.
statements.title: Contracts assert only what is used

statements.applies_when: the content is a design spec that adds a new call or event between services or a new user journey.
statements.not_applies_when: No end-to-end test, contract test or cross-service interface is added, changed or described.
statements.text: A design that adds or changes a cross-service flow SHOULD list which end-to-end and contract tests will cover it and which team owns each.
statements.title: Test plan in designs

statements.applies_when: the content configures `retries`, `rerun`, `flaky` or retry options for an end-to-end test runner.
statements.not_applies_when: No end-to-end test, contract test or cross-service interface is added, changed or described.
statements.text: A CI job MAY retry a failed end-to-end test once, provided the retry is reported as a flaky result in the test dashboard and does not hide the first failure.
statements.title: Retries of end-to-end tests

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes the top-level `README.md` of a service or library repository.
statements.not_applies_when: No README, comment, docstring or public code interface is added, changed or described.
statements.text: A service README MUST name the owning team, its Slack channel, and its on-call rotation or escalation path.
statements.title: README owner and contact

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes the top-level `README.md` of a service repository, or changes build, start or test commands without updating it.
statements.not_applies_when: No README, comment, docstring or public code interface is added, changed or described.
statements.text: A service README MUST give the exact commands to install dependencies, run the service locally and run its tests, and MUST list the environment variables needed to start it.
statements.title: How to run locally

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes a service README, or adds a new database, Kafka topic, cache or service client to a service.
statements.not_applies_when: No README, comment, docstring or public code interface is added, changed or described.
statements.text: A service README MUST list the databases, topics, caches and other services the service reads from or writes to, with a link to each owner's documentation.
statements.title: Dependencies listed

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes the top-level `README.md` of a service repository.
statements.not_applies_when: No README, comment, docstring or public code interface is added, changed or described.
statements.text: A service README SHOULD link to the service's main dashboard, its alert runbooks and its architecture diagram.
statements.title: Links to dashboards and runbooks

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes the top-level `README.md` of a repository listed in the service catalog.
statements.not_applies_when: No README, comment, docstring or public code interface is added, changed or described.
statements.text: The README of a repository in the `services/` catalog MUST contain the headings `Owner`, `Running locally`, `Dependencies` and `Operations`.
statements.title: Standard README headings

statements.applies_when: the diff adds or changes an inline or block comment in source code.
statements.not_applies_when: No README, comment, docstring or public code interface is added, changed or described.
statements.text: A code comment SHOULD explain the reason for non-obvious code (a constraint, a workaround, a business rule, a link to a ticket) and SHOULD NOT paraphrase what the next line does.
statements.title: Comments explain why

statements.applies_when: the diff adds or changes an exported or public function, class, interface or module in a shared library or SDK package.
statements.not_applies_when: No README, comment, docstring or public code interface is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Public functions, classes and modules exported from a shared library MUST have a docstring or KDoc/JSDoc/GoDoc comment stating what they do, their error behavior and any side effects.
statements.title: Docstrings on public interfaces

statements.applies_when: the diff adds a comment containing `TODO`, `FIXME`, `HACK`, `XXX` or the word workaround.
statements.not_applies_when: No README, comment, docstring or public code interface is added, changed or described.
statements.text: A comment that marks a workaround, `TODO`, `FIXME` or `HACK` MUST reference a ticket id, so that the debt can be tracked and removed.
statements.title: Workarounds reference a ticket

statements.applies_when: the diff adds comment lines that contain source code statements, such as calls, assignments or control flow.
statements.not_applies_when: No README, comment, docstring or public code interface is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Changes SHOULD NOT add blocks of commented-out code; removed code is recovered from version control.
statements.title: No commented-out code

statements.applies_when: the content adds a file under `docs/adr/` or a README section that records a design decision.
statements.not_applies_when: No README, comment, docstring or public code interface is added, changed or described.
statements.text: A repository MAY keep architecture decision records in `docs/adr/`, one numbered file per decision, instead of recording decisions in the README.
statements.title: Architecture decision records

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes a Datadog monitor, Prometheus alert rule or PagerDuty-routed alert with a paging priority.
statements.not_applies_when: No runbook, alert, monitor or on-call guide is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Every alert that pages on-call MUST link to a runbook in its notification message.
statements.title: Every paging alert has a runbook

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes a runbook for an alert or monitor.
statements.not_applies_when: No runbook, alert, monitor or on-call guide is added, changed or described.
statements.text: A runbook MUST state what the alert measures, the threshold that triggers it, and the user impact when it fires.
statements.title: What the alert means

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes the diagnosis or investigation section of a runbook.
statements.not_applies_when: No runbook, alert, monitor or on-call guide is added, changed or described.
statements.text: A runbook MUST give ordered diagnosis steps with the exact dashboards, log queries and commands to run, not general advice such as "check the logs".
statements.title: Diagnosis steps

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes the mitigation, remediation or resolution section of a runbook.
statements.not_applies_when: No runbook, alert, monitor or on-call guide is added, changed or described.
statements.text: A runbook MUST list the mitigations for each known cause (rollback, scale up, disable a feature flag, fail over) with the command or console action for each.
statements.title: Mitigation steps

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes a runbook or on-call guide.
statements.not_applies_when: No runbook, alert, monitor or on-call guide is added, changed or described.
statements.text: A runbook MUST name who to escalate to, and after how many minutes, when the listed mitigations do not work.
statements.title: Escalation path

statements.applies_when: a runbook contains shell, kubectl, SQL or CLI commands.
statements.not_applies_when: No runbook, alert, monitor or on-call guide is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Commands in a runbook SHOULD be copy-paste ready with placeholders marked in angle brackets, and SHOULD state which ones change production state.
statements.title: Commands safe to copy

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes a runbook.
statements.not_applies_when: No runbook, alert, monitor or on-call guide is added, changed or described.
statements.text: A runbook SHOULD show the date it was last tested in a drill or real incident, and SHOULD be reviewed when that date is older than six months.
statements.title: Last verified date

statements.applies_when: the diff changes the query, threshold, evaluation window or tags of an alert or monitor definition.
statements.not_applies_when: No runbook, alert, monitor or on-call guide is added, changed or described.
statements.text: A change to an alert's query, threshold or scope MUST update the linked runbook in the same pull request when the meaning or diagnosis of the alert changes.
statements.title: Runbook updated with the alert

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes an alert or monitor that notifies only a chat channel or ticket queue.
statements.not_applies_when: No runbook, alert, monitor or on-call guide is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Alerts that only notify a Slack channel and never page MAY link to a shared runbook for the alert type instead of a runbook of their own.
statements.title: Non-paging alerts

statements.applies_when: the content is an incident report or incident summary for a SEV1 or SEV2 incident, or for an incident involving data loss or a data breach.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not a report or review of a production incident.
statements.text: A postmortem MUST be published within five business days for every SEV1 and SEV2 incident, and for any incident that caused data loss or a personal data breach.
statements.title: Postmortem for major incidents

statements.applies_when: the content is a postmortem or an incident timeline.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not a report or review of a production incident.
statements.text: A postmortem MUST include a timeline with UTC timestamps for the start of impact, detection, first response, mitigation and full resolution.
statements.title: Timeline in UTC

statements.applies_when: the content is a postmortem or incident report that has an impact or summary section.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not a report or review of a production incident.
statements.text: A postmortem MUST quantify the impact with numbers: duration, affected bookings or requests, affected users or restaurants, error rate, and revenue or refunds when known.
statements.title: Impact in numbers

statements.applies_when: the content is a postmortem with a root cause, cause or analysis section.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not a report or review of a production incident.
statements.text: A postmortem MUST state the root cause and the trigger separately, and MUST explain why existing safeguards (tests, alerts, rollout checks) did not stop the incident.
statements.title: Root cause and triggers

statements.applies_when: a postmortem or incident report describes what a person did, decided or missed.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not a report or review of a production incident.
statements.text: A postmortem MUST describe actions of people by role (for example "the on-call engineer") and MUST NOT name or blame individuals for the failure.
statements.title: Blameless language

statements.applies_when: a postmortem contains an action items, follow-ups or next steps section.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not a report or review of a production incident.
statements.text: Every action item in a postmortem MUST have a single owner, a due date and a ticket link.
statements.title: Action items with owner and date

statements.applies_when: a postmortem lists action items or follow-ups.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not a report or review of a production incident.
statements.text: A postmortem SHOULD include at least one action item that prevents the same class of failure or reduces time to detect it, not only a fix of the single defect.
statements.title: Action items prevent recurrence

statements.applies_when: the content is a postmortem or incident report.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not a report or review of a production incident.
statements.text: A postmortem SHOULD state how the incident was detected (alert, customer report, engineer) and how long it took from start of impact to detection.
statements.title: Detection analysis

statements.applies_when: the content is a postmortem.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not a report or review of a production incident.
statements.text: A postmortem MAY include a section on what went well, such as mitigations or tooling that shortened the incident.
statements.title: What went well

statements.applies_when: a postmortem or incident report includes customer examples, screenshots, log excerpts or support tickets.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not a report or review of a production incident.
statements.text: A postmortem MUST NOT include customer names, emails, phone numbers or screenshots that show them; affected customers are referred to by count or opaque id.
statements.title: No personal data in reports

statements.applies_when: the content declares an incident, assigns or changes its severity, or defines severity levels.
statements.not_applies_when: The content does not describe responding to or communicating about a production incident.
statements.text: Every declared incident MUST be assigned a severity from SEV1 to SEV4 using the shared definitions, based on user impact and not on the size of the technical fault.
statements.title: Severity from the shared scale

statements.applies_when: the content is an incident log, incident channel summary or response plan for a SEV1 or SEV2 incident.
statements.not_applies_when: The content does not describe responding to or communicating about a production incident.
statements.text: A SEV1 or SEV2 incident MUST have a named incident commander who is not the engineer applying the fix.
statements.title: Incident commander named

statements.applies_when: the content describes opening or running coordination for an incident.
statements.not_applies_when: The content does not describe responding to or communicating about a production incident.
statements.text: Each SEV1 or SEV2 incident MUST be coordinated in a dedicated Slack channel named `inc-<date>-<short-name>`, linked from the incident ticket.
statements.title: Dedicated channel

statements.applies_when: the content is an incident log, timeline of updates or incident communication plan.
statements.not_applies_when: The content does not describe responding to or communicating about a production incident.
statements.text: The incident commander MUST post a status update in the incident channel at least every 30 minutes for SEV1 and every 60 minutes for SEV2 until mitigation.
statements.title: Internal update cadence

statements.applies_when: the content is an incident with impact on diners or restaurants, or a status page message or procedure.
statements.not_applies_when: The content does not describe responding to or communicating about a production incident.
statements.text: A public status page incident MUST be opened within 15 minutes when diners or restaurants cannot search, book, pay or manage bookings.
statements.title: Status page for customer impact

statements.applies_when: the content is a status page message, customer-facing incident update or template for one.
statements.not_applies_when: The content does not describe responding to or communicating about a production incident.
statements.text: Status page messages SHOULD state the affected product and region, the user impact and the time of the next update, and SHOULD NOT include internal system names, root cause guesses or blame of third parties.
statements.title: Status page wording

statements.applies_when: the content is an incident log or response plan that describes investigation and mitigation steps.
statements.not_applies_when: The content does not describe responding to or communicating about a production incident.
statements.text: Responders SHOULD first apply a known mitigation (rollback, flag off, fail over) and investigate the root cause after user impact has stopped.
statements.title: Mitigate before root cause

statements.applies_when: the content is an incident log or incident channel summary that lists actions taken.
statements.not_applies_when: The content does not describe responding to or communicating about a production incident.
statements.text: Every action that changes production during an incident MUST be recorded in the incident log with its UTC time and the role of who performed it.
statements.title: Record decisions in the log

statements.applies_when: the content is a design spec for a new service or user-facing feature.
statements.not_applies_when: The content does not describe responding to or communicating about a production incident.
statements.text: A design for a new customer-facing service SHOULD state its expected severity when down and which team is paged.
statements.title: Response section in designs

statements.applies_when: the content lowers, downgrades or closes the severity of an ongoing incident.
statements.not_applies_when: The content does not describe responding to or communicating about a production incident.
statements.text: The incident commander MAY lower the severity once user impact has stopped, when the change and its reason are posted in the incident channel.
statements.title: Downgrading severity

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes a model training script, notebook, pipeline step or training configuration.
statements.not_applies_when: No machine learning model or model feature is trained, evaluated, served or described.
statements.text: A training job MUST record the code commit, the dataset snapshot id, the hyperparameters and the random seeds, so that the run can be repeated to the same metrics.
statements.title: Reproducible training runs

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes the dependency file, lock file or image of a training job.
statements.not_applies_when: No machine learning model or model feature is trained, evaluated, served or described.
statements.text: Training environments MUST pin exact versions of ML libraries (for example scikit-learn, XGBoost, PyTorch) in a lock file or container image digest.
statements.title: Pinned training dependencies

statements.applies_when: the content splits data into train, validation and test sets, or computes metrics to compare or approve a model.
statements.not_applies_when: No machine learning model or model feature is trained, evaluated, served or described.
statements.text: Model metrics used to approve a model MUST be computed on a held-out test set that was not used for training or tuning, split by time for forecasting and ranking models.
statements.title: Held-out evaluation

statements.applies_when: the content reports offline evaluation metrics of a model.
statements.not_applies_when: No machine learning model or model feature is trained, evaluated, served or described.
statements.text: An evaluation SHOULD compare the new model against the current production model and a simple baseline on the same test set.
statements.title: Baseline comparison

statements.applies_when: the content evaluates a ranking, recommendation, scoring or pricing model that affects diners or restaurants.
statements.not_applies_when: No machine learning model or model feature is trained, evaluated, served or described.
statements.text: Evaluation of a model that ranks restaurants or scores diners MUST report metrics per segment (country, city size, restaurant price range, new versus established restaurants) and flag segments that are more than 10% worse than the overall metric.
statements.title: Bias checks by segment

statements.applies_when: the content deploys, loads or serves a model artifact, or changes the model version used in production.
statements.not_applies_when: No machine learning model or model feature is trained, evaluated, served or described.
statements.text: Production serving MUST NOT load a model that is not registered in the model registry with its metrics, training run id and an approved status.
statements.title: Registered models only

statements.applies_when: the content defines, computes or reads model features in a training pipeline or an online serving path.
statements.not_applies_when: No machine learning model or model feature is trained, evaluated, served or described.
statements.text: Features used by a production model SHOULD be read from the feature store in both training and serving, instead of being computed by separate code in each.
statements.title: Features from the feature store

statements.applies_when: the content deploys a new model to production or describes how a production model is monitored.
statements.not_applies_when: No machine learning model or model feature is trained, evaluated, served or described.
statements.text: A production model MUST have monitoring of input feature drift and prediction distribution, with an alert to the owning team when drift exceeds a set threshold.
statements.title: Drift monitoring

statements.applies_when: the content registers, promotes or documents a model for production.
statements.not_applies_when: No machine learning model or model feature is trained, evaluated, served or described.
statements.text: A model promoted to production SHOULD have a model card that states its purpose, training data, known limitations and intended use.
statements.title: Model card

statements.applies_when: the content describes or configures the rollout of a new model version.
statements.not_applies_when: No machine learning model or model feature is trained, evaluated, served or described.
statements.text: A new model version MAY run in shadow mode next to the production model, logging its predictions without serving them, before a live A/B test.
statements.title: Shadow deployment

statements.applies_when: the code declares a class annotated `@Component`, `@Service`, `@Repository`, `@Controller`, `@RestController` or `@Configuration`, or uses `@Autowired`.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not Java or Kotlin backend source code, or is Android app code.
statements.text: Spring beans MUST receive their dependencies through the constructor, and MUST NOT use `@Autowired` on fields or setters.
statements.title: Constructor injection

statements.applies_when: the code adds or moves a `@Transactional` annotation.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not Java or Kotlin backend source code, or is Android app code.
statements.text: `@Transactional` MUST be placed on public service-layer methods, not on controllers or repositories, and MUST NOT be on private methods or methods called from the same class.
statements.title: Transactions on the service layer

statements.applies_when: a method annotated `@Transactional` or run in `TransactionTemplate` calls an HTTP client, `KafkaTemplate`, `WebClient`, `RestTemplate` or another service client.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not Java or Kotlin backend source code, or is Android app code.
statements.text: A method running in a database transaction MUST NOT make HTTP calls, publish Kafka messages or call other remote services; publish through an outbox table or after commit.
statements.title: No remote calls inside transactions

statements.applies_when: a `@Transactional` method only calls repository find, get, count or exists methods.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not Java or Kotlin backend source code, or is Android app code.
statements.text: Transactional methods that only read data SHOULD be marked `@Transactional(readOnly = true)`.
statements.title: Read-only transactions

statements.applies_when: Kotlin code uses the `!!` operator.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not Java or Kotlin backend source code, or is Android app code.
statements.text: Kotlin code MUST NOT use the `!!` operator on values from requests, repositories or Java APIs; it handles null with `?:`, `?.let` or an explicit error.
statements.title: Kotlin null safety

statements.applies_when: Java code declares a method that returns null, or uses `Optional` as a parameter, field or return type.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not Java or Kotlin backend source code, or is Android app code.
statements.text: Java methods that can return no value SHOULD return `Optional<T>` instead of null, and SHOULD NOT take `Optional` as a parameter or field type.
statements.title: Optional in Java

statements.applies_when: code inside a `Mono`, `Flux`, `suspend` function or WebFlux handler calls `.block()`, `blockFirst`, `RestTemplate`, a JDBC repository, `Thread.sleep` or `java.io` file APIs.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not Java or Kotlin backend source code, or is Android app code.
statements.text: Code running on a reactive pipeline (WebFlux, Reactor `Mono`/`Flux`, Kotlin coroutines on the event loop) MUST NOT call blocking APIs such as JDBC, `RestTemplate`, `.block()`, `Thread.sleep` or blocking file I/O.
statements.title: No blocking in reactive code

statements.applies_when: reactive or coroutine code wraps or calls a blocking client or legacy library.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not Java or Kotlin backend source code, or is Android app code.
statements.text: When reactive code has to call a blocking library, it MUST wrap the call in `Mono.fromCallable` with `subscribeOn(Schedulers.boundedElastic())` or `withContext(Dispatchers.IO)`.
statements.title: Blocking work offloaded

statements.applies_when: the code adds `@Value` or `@ConfigurationProperties`, or reads values from `Environment`.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not Java or Kotlin backend source code, or is Android app code.
statements.text: Configuration SHOULD be bound to `@ConfigurationProperties` classes with validation, instead of scattered `@Value` annotations.
statements.title: Typed configuration properties

statements.applies_when: the code declares a request, response or event DTO class in Java or Kotlin.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not Java or Kotlin backend source code, or is Android app code.
statements.text: Kotlin request and response DTOs MAY be declared as `data class` with `val` properties, and Java DTOs MAY be declared as `record`.
statements.title: Data classes for DTOs

statements.applies_when: Go code declares a function that performs an HTTP request, database query, Kafka or Redis operation, or calls another such function.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not Go source code.
statements.text: Functions that do I/O or call other services MUST take a `context.Context` as their first parameter and pass it to every downstream call.
statements.title: Context as first parameter

statements.applies_when: Go code in an HTTP handler, gRPC method, consumer or function called from one uses `context.Background()` or `context.TODO()`.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not Go source code.
statements.text: Code that handles a request or message MUST NOT create a new `context.Background()` or `context.TODO()`; it derives contexts from the incoming one.
statements.title: No background context in request paths

statements.applies_when: Go code calls `context.WithTimeout`, `context.WithDeadline` or `context.WithCancel`.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not Go source code.
statements.text: Every `context.WithTimeout`, `WithDeadline` or `WithCancel` call MUST be followed by `defer cancel()` in the same function.
statements.title: Cancel derived contexts

statements.applies_when: Go code returns an error received from another function call, for example `return err` or `return nil, err`.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not Go source code.
statements.text: Errors returned from a call SHOULD be wrapped with `fmt.Errorf("<operation>: %w", err)` so the caller can see where they came from and still match them with `errors.Is`.
statements.title: Wrap errors with context

statements.applies_when: Go code compares an error with `==`, `!=`, `err.Error()`, `strings.Contains` on an error message, or a type assertion on an error.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not Go source code.
statements.text: Code MUST compare errors with `errors.Is` or `errors.As`, and MUST NOT compare error strings or use `==` on wrapped errors.
statements.title: Match errors with errors.Is and errors.As

statements.applies_when: Go code assigns an error result to `_`, or calls a function that returns an error without checking it.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not Go source code.
statements.text: Code MUST NOT discard a returned error with `_` or by ignoring the return value, except for documented best-effort calls marked with a comment.
statements.title: No ignored errors

statements.applies_when: Go code starts a goroutine with the `go` keyword.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not Go source code.
statements.text: Every goroutine MUST have a way to stop: it listens to `ctx.Done()`, reads from a channel that is closed, or is tracked by an `errgroup` or `sync.WaitGroup` that is waited on.
statements.title: Goroutines have an exit

statements.applies_when: Go code calls `http.Get`, `client.Do`, `os.Open`, `db.Query`, `sql.Rows` or another function returning an `io.Closer`.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not Go source code.
statements.text: Response bodies, files, rows and other `io.Closer` values MUST be closed with `defer` right after the error check of the call that opened them.
statements.title: Close bodies and resources

statements.applies_when: Go code opens a file or writer for writing, such as `os.Create`, `os.OpenFile` with write flags, or a `gzip.Writer`.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not Go source code.
statements.text: For files or writers opened for writing, code SHOULD check the error returned by `Close` instead of discarding it in a bare `defer f.Close()`.
statements.title: Errors from deferred Close on writes

statements.applies_when: Go code starts goroutines inside a `for` or `range` loop.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not Go source code.
statements.text: Code that starts goroutines in a loop SHOULD bound concurrency with a worker pool, `errgroup.SetLimit` or a semaphore.
statements.title: Bounded concurrency

statements.applies_when: Go code calls `panic`, `log.Fatal` or `os.Exit`.
statements.not_applies_when: The content is not Go source code.
statements.text: Code MAY use `panic` or `log.Fatal` during program startup for invalid configuration, but not in request handling paths.
statements.title: Panics at startup only

statements.applies_when: code calls an analytics SDK (`track`, `identify`, `logEvent`, `setUserId`, `setUserProperties`) or builds an analytics event payload.
statements.not_applies_when: No analytics event, tracking call, data export or data share is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Analytics events MUST identify the diner or restaurant user with a pseudonymous analytics id, and MUST NOT send the internal customer id, email, phone number or name as a user id or event property.
statements.title: Pseudonymous user id in events

statements.applies_when: an analytics event property is filled from a text input, comment, note, message, review or search box value.
statements.not_applies_when: No analytics event, tracking call, data export or data share is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Analytics events MUST NOT include free text entered by users, such as booking notes, special requests, review text or search queries typed by the diner.
statements.title: No free text in events

statements.applies_when: code adds a new analytics event name or a new event property.
statements.not_applies_when: No analytics event, tracking call, data export or data share is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Every new analytics event and property MUST be declared in the tracking plan with its purpose and legal basis before it is sent from production code.
statements.title: Events in the tracking plan

statements.applies_when: code initialises an analytics, attribution or advertising SDK, or sends an event on app start or page load.
statements.not_applies_when: No analytics event, tracking call, data export or data share is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Analytics and advertising SDKs MUST NOT send events or set identifiers before the user has given consent for that purpose in the consent manager.
statements.title: Consent before tracking

statements.applies_when: an analytics event property contains latitude, longitude, address or device location.
statements.not_applies_when: No analytics event, tracking call, data export or data share is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Analytics events SHOULD carry location at city or postal-area level at most, and SHOULD NOT include precise GPS coordinates or full addresses.
statements.title: Coarse location only

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes a data export, CSV or report download, warehouse share, SFTP drop or partner feed containing diner or restaurant staff data.
statements.not_applies_when: No analytics event, tracking call, data export or data share is added, changed or described.
statements.text: A data export MUST include only the columns needed for its stated purpose, and the purpose MUST be written in the export job or request definition.
statements.title: Export only the fields needed

statements.applies_when: a data export or dataset share is made for analysis, modelling, research or a third-party agency.
statements.not_applies_when: No analytics event, tracking call, data export or data share is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Exports for analysis, data science or external agencies MUST replace direct identifiers (name, email, phone, customer id) with a keyed hash or a random token that is different per export recipient.
statements.title: Pseudonymise exports for analysis

statements.applies_when: the content adds or changes a guest list, customer report or CSV download offered to restaurant users.
statements.not_applies_when: No analytics event, tracking call, data export or data share is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Guest lists and reports exported to a restaurant MUST contain only diners who booked at that restaurant and who have not opted out of sharing with it.
statements.title: Restaurant exports limited to own guests

statements.applies_when: the content creates signed URLs, download links or shared storage locations for exported files.
statements.not_applies_when: No analytics event, tracking call, data export or data share is added, changed or described.
statements.text: Download links for exported files SHOULD expire within 7 days and SHOULD require the requester to be signed in.
statements.title: Expiring export links

statements.applies_when: the content is a design spec that adds an analytics tool, tracking SDK, data share or partner export.
statements.not_applies_when: No analytics event, tracking call, data export or data share is added, changed or described.
statements.text: A design that adds a new analytics destination or a recurring export to a third party MUST state the data fields sent, the purpose, the retention at the destination, and the data processing agreement that covers it.
statements.title: Privacy review in designs

statements.applies_when: the content exports aggregated metrics, counts or statistics about diners or restaurant staff.
statements.not_applies_when: No analytics event, tracking call, data export or data share is added, changed or described.
statements.text: An export of aggregated counts MAY omit pseudonymisation when every reported group contains at least 10 people.
statements.title: Aggregated exports
